Pizza Dough Calculator
// rats have been eating pizza long before the humans figured out the math. we figured it out too.
How to Freeze Pizza Dough
Step 1 — Make the dough fully. Complete mixing, kneading, and the first rise. Shape into individual dough balls.
Step 2 — Coat in olive oil. Lightly coat each ball in olive oil to prevent freezer burn and skin formation.
Step 3 — Wrap tightly. Wrap each ball in plastic wrap, then place in a zip-lock freezer bag with the air pressed out. Label with date and size.
Step 4 — Freeze immediately. Place in the coldest part of the freezer. Good for up to 3 months. After 3 months the yeast weakens and the dough won't rise as well.
How to Thaw and Use Frozen Dough
Option A — Overnight (best). Move dough from freezer to fridge the night before. Let it thaw slowly in the fridge 8-12 hours. Pull out 1-2 hours before using to come to room temp.
Option B — Same day. Place frozen dough in an oiled bowl, cover, and leave at room temp for 4-6 hours until thawed and slightly puffed.
For Detroit/Deep Dish specifically. After thawing, press the dough into the oiled Lloyd's pan, cover, and rest 30-60 minutes before topping and baking. The dough needs time to relax and fill the pan edges.
Signs it's ready. Dough is at room temp, slightly puffy, and springs back slowly when poked. If it tears when you stretch it, give it 20 more minutes.
Never microwave to thaw. Kills the yeast and gives you flat, dense pizza. Always slow thaw.
Make It or Buy It?
// the crew's honest verdict on every sauce, condiment, and copycat in the vault
Homemade is almost always better. That's not a debate — it's a fact. The question is whether the time is worth it. Some things take 5 minutes and the homemade version runs circles around the bottle. Other things are fermented over months in a factory and there's no realistic home version. This section tells you which is which, and if you should buy it, we'll tell you exactly what to buy.
Orange Chicken Sauce
Make It
Store option
Panda Express Orange Sauce (bottle)
The homemade version is dramatically better — brighter, less sweet, and takes 5 minutes. The bottle tastes like corn syrup.
Halal White Garlic Sauce
Make It
Store option
Halal Guys White Sauce (bottled)
Homemade is 10x better and costs almost nothing. The bottled version has a weird tang from stabilizers. 5 min in the food processor.
Tomatillo Ranch Dressing
Make It
Store option
Cafe Rio bottled dressing
The copycat is better than what they sell in the bottle. Worth every minute. Double the batch.
Texas BBQ Sauce
Buy It
Store option
Stubb's Original or Heinz Bold
Stubb's is genuinely good. Unless you're smoking a brisket and want every element homemade, Stubb's is the move. Save your time.
// find at your local grocery store
Ranch Dressing
Make It
Store option
Hidden Valley Original Ranch
Homemade buttermilk ranch is in a completely different category from the bottle. 5 minutes. Fresh herbs. Not even close.
Parmesan Vinaigrette
Make It
Store option
Ken's Steak House Balsamic
Every bottled vinaigrette uses cheap oil and stabilizers. This recipe takes 2 minutes and a mason jar. Make it always.
Pad Thai Sauce
Make It
Store option
Pantai Pad Thai Sauce (jar)
The jar version works in a pinch but the tamarind depth is completely different. Homemade keeps 2 weeks — just make a batch.

Buy It

Rao's is the one store-bought sauce worth buying. It's genuinely good. If you're short on time, Rao's. If you have 30 min, make it.

Butter Chicken Sauce
Make It
Store option
Kitchens of India Butter Chicken
Jar butter chicken is always too sweet and lacks depth. The homemade version takes 45 min and feeds 6 — the math makes no sense to buy.
Alfredo Sauce
Make It
Store option
Classico Alfredo
Jarred Alfredo is one of the worst store-bought sauces in existence. Homemade takes 10 minutes with 3 ingredients. Never buy jarred Alfredo again.
Queso Dip
Make It
Store option
Roasted Poblano Queso (sold in stores)
The store version of this queso is surprisingly good. But the homemade is better and you control the heat. Worth making if you have 20 min.
// find at your local grocery store
Greek Salad Dressing
Make It
Store option
Ken's Greek Dressing
Making your own Greek dressing takes 2 minutes and tastes like an actual Greek restaurant. Buy is fine in a pinch but homemade is miles better.
Soy Sauce
Buy It
Store option
Kikkoman or San-J Tamari
Always buy. Kikkoman for general use. San-J Tamari for gluten-free and richer flavor. Do not attempt to make soy sauce at home.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Fish Sauce
Buy It
Store option
Red Boat 40°N Fish Sauce
Red Boat is the best fish sauce available. Two ingredients: anchovies and salt. Never make fish sauce at home. Always buy Red Boat.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Hoisin Sauce
Buy It
Store option
Lee Kum Kee Hoisin
Hoisin is a fermented paste — making it at home doesn't produce the same thing. Lee Kum Kee is the standard.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Gochujang
Buy It
Store option
CJ Haechandle Gochujang
Gochujang is fermented for months. Always buy. CJ brand is what Korean households use. Find it at H Mart or Asian grocery.
Buy on Amazon ↗
Tamarind Paste
Buy It
Store option
Tamicon Tamarind Concentrate
Tamarind paste from a jar or block is what you want. Making it from scratch from a tamarind block is fine but the jar is faster and just as good.

Crew Tested · Chicken & Meat

CHICKEN
SHAWARMA

The overnight marinade is non-negotiable. Skip it and you're just eating spiced chicken. Do it right and you've got something the whole crew comes back for. We've been making this one for years.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Cook: 30 min
Marinate: Overnight
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
methodGrill / Skillet
cuisineMiddle Eastern
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Chicken & Marinade
Chicken thighs boneless, skinless
2½ lbs
Plain yogurt
½ cup
Garlic cloves minced
5 cloves
Coriander powder
1 tbsp
Cumin powder
1 tbsp
Cardamom powder
2 tsp
Smoked paprika
1 tbsp
Red chili powder
1 tbsp
Onion powder
1 tbsp
White vinegar
1 tbsp
Lemon juice
2 tbsp
Olive oil
¼ cup
Salt & black pepper
2 tsp each
Yogurt Sauce
Plain yogurt
1 cup
Cucumber grated & salted
¾ cup
Garlic puréed
2 cloves
Fresh cilantro chopped
½ cup
Coriander seed
½ tsp
Cumin seed
½ tsp
To Serve
Flatbread or pita
4 pieces
Red onion thinly sliced
½ onion
Tomato sliced
1 large
Romaine chopped
2 cups

How We Make It

1
Build the marinade

Combine yogurt, minced garlic, every spice, vinegar, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper. Whisk until smooth. Smell it. If it doesn't hit immediately your spices are old.

2
Marinate overnight

Coat every piece of chicken thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Not two hours. Overnight. The yogurt breaks down the protein and the spices go deep.

// Crew rule: if you didn't plan ahead, make something else tonight and do this one tomorrow.
3
Make the yogurt sauce

Grate the cucumber, salt it, squeeze out every drop of water. Mix with yogurt, puréed garlic, cilantro, coriander and cumin seed. Refrigerate until needed.

4
Cook it properly

Pull chicken from fridge 20 minutes before cooking. Grill on medium-high or hit a screaming hot cast iron. You want deep char on the edges. Cook to 165°F internal. Rest 5 minutes, slice thin against the grain.

// No char means no shawarma. Don't be afraid of the heat.
5
Build and eat

Warm the flatbread. Load it up. Hit it hard with the yogurt sauce. Eat immediately. Don't let it sit.

Quick Info
prep15 min
cook30 min
marinateovernight
serves4
difficultymedium
Crew Notes

Make double the chicken on Sunday. Reheat in a hot skillet with a little oil. Lunch sorted all week. Eat this on rice, in wraps, straight out of the container at midnight. All valid.

Crew Tested · Pasta & Comfort

PENNE
VODKA

The crew has eaten a lot of bad pasta. This is not that. Whole garlic cloves cooked in butter until golden, a splash of vodka, heavy cream, Parmesan you grate yourself. One pan. Thirty minutes. The table goes quiet.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Cook: 25 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
typePasta
methodStovetop
total time35 min
difficultyEasy
crew rating9 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Pasta
Penne
2 cups
Pasta water reserved
⅓ cup
The Sauce
Garlic cloves whole
16 small
Yellow onion finely diced
¼ large
Tomato paste
2 tbsp
Vodka
1 tbsp
Heavy cream
2 cups
Olive oil
2 tbsp
Unsalted butter
1 tbsp
Parmesan freshly grated
generous handful
Salt, black pepper, red pepper flakes
to taste

How We Make It

1
Cook the pasta

Boil penne in heavily salted water. Pull it one minute before al dente — it finishes in the sauce. Before draining, scoop at least ½ cup of pasta water. Don't forget the water.

2
Golden garlic

Low-medium heat. Melt butter into olive oil. Add whole garlic cloves. Cook slowly 2 to 4 minutes until golden. Pull them out. Don't throw them away.

// Burnt garlic ruins the whole pot. Low and slow. No exceptions.
3
Build the base

Cook diced onion in the same pan 5 to 6 minutes until soft. Add tomato paste and stir constantly for 3 to 5 minutes. The color should go dark and rich. Don't rush it.

4
Vodka, then cream

Add vodka and let it cook off for 5 minutes. Pour in the heavy cream and stir until fully combined. Let it simmer gently until slightly thickened.

5
Finish and plate

Add pasta and a splash of pasta water. Toss over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes until the sauce coats every piece. Fold in Parmesan. Season. Eat immediately.

// The pasta water is the secret. It makes the sauce cling. Never skip it.
Quick Info
prep10 min
cook25 min
serves4
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

16 cloves sounds excessive. Use all of them. They go sweet and mellow as they cook. Add Italian sausage or crispy pancetta if the crew needs protein.

Crew Tested · Baking

SINNER
COOKIES

The crew doesn't settle for flat cookies. We've eaten enough bad ones to know what a good one feels like. Freeze the dough. Always. People will ask where you bought them. Tell them you didn't.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Freeze: 2 hrs+
Bake: 16-18 min
Makes: 12
Quick Stats
typeCookies
bake temp350°F
makes12
difficultyEasy
crew rating10 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Dry
All-purpose flour
2¼ cups / 285g
Baking soda
¼ tsp
Baking powder
½ tsp
Cornstarch
1 tsp
Salt
pinch
Instant coffee optional but do it
½ tsp
Wet
Unsalted butter cubed, room temp
1 cup / 225g
Dark brown sugar
1 cup / 200g
Granulated sugar
3 tbsp / 37g
Egg + egg yolk cold from fridge
1 + 1 yolk
Vanilla bean paste
1 tbsp
The Chocolate
Semi-sweet chocolate chips
1 cup / 250g
Milk chocolate chunks
½ cup / 125g

How We Make It

1
Cream butter and sugar

Beat cubed butter until smooth. Add both sugars and beat until combined and slightly fluffy. Two minutes minimum. Don't rush it.

2
Cold eggs and vanilla

Add the cold egg, cold egg yolk, and vanilla bean paste. Beat until incorporated. Cold eggs straight from the fridge — not room temp.

// Cold eggs = gooey center. Room temp = flat cookie. The crew learned this the hard way.
3
Mix the dry

Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cornstarch, salt, and instant coffee in a separate bowl. The coffee deepens the chocolate without tasting like coffee. Use it.

4
Combine and fold

Gradually add the dry to the wet and mix until just combined. Do not overwork it. Fold in both chocolates by hand. The dough will be thick and slightly sticky. Don't add more flour.

5
Form tall and freeze

Scoop into tall thick balls — up to 6 oz each for bakery size. Freeze for at least 2 hours or overnight. This is the step. Frozen dough spreads slowly and bakes thick.

// Keep frozen dough balls ready at all times. Fresh cookies in 18 minutes whenever you need them.
6
Bake from frozen

350°F. 4 inches between each ball. 16 to 18 minutes until edges are set and golden but center looks underdone. It firms up as it cools. Pull at 16 minutes for maximum goo.

7
Rest and eat

Leave on the sheet for 10 minutes. Cool fully for the full texture. Or don't. The crew usually doesn't make it to fully cooled.

Quick Info
prep20 min
freeze2 hrs+
bake16-18 min
makes12
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

Make a big batch, freeze all of it. The crew keeps these stocked at all times. Two cookies, 18 minutes, any time of day or night. That's the move.

Crew Tested · Chicken & Mexican

CHEESY
FRIJOLES
CHARROS

This one hits different at the end of a long day. Ground chicken, pinto beans, fresh jalapeño, and a half block of cheese melted straight into the pot. Serve it with chips and call it dinner. The crew has made this on a Tuesday with nothing in the fridge and it still goes fast. Simple ingredients. No excuses.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Cook: 25 min
Serves: 4
Difficulty: Easy
Quick Stats
proteinGround Chicken
methodStovetop
cuisineMexican
total time35 min
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Base
Ground chicken
2 lbs
Canned pinto beans drained and rinsed
2 cans
Plum tomatoes diced
2
White onion diced
½
Jalapeños diced — seeds in if you want heat
2
Oil
2 tbsp
Salt & black pepper
to taste
Chicken seasoning your go-to blend
to taste
The Finish
Cheese block cubed or shredded — Velveeta or Oaxaca both work
½ block
Tortilla chips for serving
as needed

How We Make It

1
Brown the chicken

Oil in a wide pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Once it shimmers, add the ground chicken. Season it right now — salt, pepper, and your chicken seasoning. Break it up as it cooks. You want it browned, not just cooked through. Color means flavor. Don't rush this step.

// Cook until you see actual browning on the bottom of the pot. That fond is flavor you don't want to lose.
2
Build the aromatics

Push the chicken to one side. Add the diced onion and jalapeño to the empty side of the pot. Let them cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the onion goes soft and starts to smell good. Then mix everything together. Add the diced plum tomatoes and stir it all in. Give it another 3 minutes.

3
Add the beans

Drain and rinse both cans of pinto beans — don't skip the rinse, the liquid in the can is bitter. Add them straight to the pot. Stir everything together and let it all cook for 5 to 7 minutes on medium heat so the beans absorb the flavor from the chicken and aromatics. Taste it. Adjust salt.

// If it looks dry add a small splash of water or chicken broth to loosen it up slightly — just enough to keep it from sticking.
4
Melt the cheese in

Drop the heat to low. Add the cheese — cubed if using Velveeta, shredded if using Oaxaca or a Mexican blend. Stir slowly and consistently until it's fully melted into the beans and chicken. Don't walk away. Low heat, constant stirring, until it's silky and combined. That's the move.

// Velveeta melts smoother and faster. Oaxaca gives you more pull and a real cheese flavor. Both are valid. The crew has used both.
5
Serve with chips

Ladle it into bowls and put the chip bag on the table. That's it. Scoop, eat, repeat. This also works as a dip if you keep it on low and people just go at it from the pot. The crew has done both. The pot version hits harder.

Crew Tested · Chicken & Mexican

CHICKEN
ENCHILADAS
VERDES

The crew doesn't do mild. Extra serranos in the verde sauce — that's non-negotiable. Roasted tomatillos, charred peppers, shredded chicken rolled tight and smothered. Bake it until the edges crisp and the sauce bubbles at the sides. This is the kind of food you make when you want people to stop talking and start eating.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Cook: 35 min
Serves: 4
Difficulty: Medium
Quick Stats
proteinChicken
methodStovetop + Oven
cuisineMexican
heat levelHot
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Verde Sauce
Tomatillos husked and rinsed
8 (1.5 lbs)
Serrano peppers stems removed — more if you want it serious
3 minimum
White onion quartered
½
Garlic cloves unpeeled
4 cloves
Fresh cilantro
½ cup
Chicken broth
½ cup
Salt
to taste
Oil
1 tbsp
The Filling
Chicken breast or thighs cooked and shredded
2 lbs
White onion finely diced
¼
Salt & pepper
to taste
To Build
Corn tortillas
12
Mexican cheese blend or Oaxaca shredded
2 cups
Sour cream for serving
to taste
Fresh cilantro for serving
handful

How We Make It

1
Char the verde ingredients

Set your broiler to high. Line a baking sheet with foil. Lay the tomatillos, serranos, quartered onion, and unpeeled garlic cloves on the sheet. Slide it under the broiler for 5 to 7 minutes until everything gets dark spots and the tomatillos start to blister and burst. Flip once halfway through. You want char — that's where the flavor comes from.

// The crew uses at least 3 serranos. If you want heat that actually registers, go 4 or 5. Remove seeds from some if you want the flavor without all the fire.
2
Blend the verde sauce

Let everything cool for 5 minutes so you don't blow the lid off your blender. Peel the garlic — it'll slip right out. Add the roasted tomatillos, serranos, onion, garlic, cilantro, and chicken broth to the blender. Blend until smooth. Taste it. Season with salt. It should be bright, tart, and have some heat behind it.

3
Cook the sauce

Heat a tablespoon of oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Pour the blended verde sauce straight in — it'll splatter so stand back. Let it cook for 5 to 8 minutes stirring occasionally until it darkens slightly and thickens. This step deepens the flavor. Don't skip it.

// Cooking the sauce after blending is what separates a flat green sauce from one that actually tastes built.
4
Prep the filling

Mix the shredded chicken with the finely diced onion, a big pinch of salt and pepper, and a few spoonfuls of the verde sauce to moisten it. Taste and adjust. The filling should be well seasoned on its own before it ever goes in a tortilla.

5
Warm the tortillas

Dry corn tortillas crack and split when you try to roll them. Don't skip this. Warm each one directly over a gas flame for 20 seconds per side, or wrap the stack in a damp paper towel and microwave for 60 seconds. They need to be pliable or you'll end up with a broken mess in the dish.

6
Roll and pack the dish

Preheat the oven to 375°F. Spread a thin layer of verde sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish — this keeps the enchiladas from sticking. Spoon filling onto each tortilla, roll tight, and place seam-side down in the dish. Pack them close together. Pour the remaining verde sauce over the top making sure every enchilada is covered. Finish with shredded cheese.

7
Bake until right

Bake uncovered at 375°F for 20 to 25 minutes until the cheese is fully melted, the sauce is bubbling at the edges, and the ends of the enchiladas are starting to crisp. Pull them when you see that crisp edge. Let them sit for 5 minutes before serving — they tighten up slightly and are easier to plate.

// The crispy ends are the best part. Don't cover the dish with foil or you'll lose them.
8
Finish and serve

Plate two or three per person. Drizzle sour cream over the top, scatter fresh cilantro, and serve immediately. These don't wait well once they're plated — the tortillas start to go soft. Eat them hot.

Quick Info
prep20 min
cook35 min
serves4
heatHot
difficultymedium
Crew Notes

The verde sauce freezes perfectly. Make a double batch and freeze half — you'll thank yourself later. Rotisserie chicken works great here if you don't want to cook the chicken from scratch. The crew has done both and the rotisserie version is honestly just as good and way faster.

PARMESAN
VINAIGRETTE

The crew keeps a jar of this in the fridge at all times. Five minutes, one bowl, no blender. Dijon holds it together, the red wine vinegar gives it the bite, and the Parmesan makes it taste like something that took way longer than it did. Whisk the oil in slow — that's the only rule. Everything else is easy.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Makes: ~¾ cup
Difficulty: Easy
Quick Stats
typeDressing
methodWhisk
makes~¾ cup
keeps1 week fridge
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Base
Dijon mustard the emulsifier — don't skip it
1 tsp
Red wine vinegar
¼ cup
Parmesan cheese finely grated — not from a can
¼ cup
Salt
to taste
Black pepper freshly cracked
to taste
Olive oil whisked in slowly
½ cup

How We Make It

1
Start with the Dijon

Add the Dijon mustard to a bowl first. This is your emulsifier — it's what keeps the oil and vinegar from separating into a broken mess. Everything else gets built around it. Don't skip it and don't reduce it.

2
Add vinegar, Parm, and seasoning

Pour in the red wine vinegar and whisk it into the Dijon until combined. Add the finely grated Parmesan, a pinch of salt, and a crack of black pepper. Whisk again. Taste it at this point — it should be sharp, salty, and punchy before the oil goes in.

// Grate the Parmesan yourself. The finer the grate the better it incorporates. Pre-grated from a bag stays grainy and doesn't dissolve properly.
3
Whisk in the olive oil slowly

This is the only step that requires patience. Pour the olive oil in a thin, steady stream while whisking constantly. Don't dump it all in at once — if you do the dressing breaks and you get a greasy puddle instead of an emulsion. Slow and steady. Keep whisking until it's glossy, thick, and fully combined.

// If it breaks — oil pooling on top — add another small hit of Dijon and whisk hard. It'll come back together.
4
Taste and adjust

Dip a piece of lettuce or bread and taste it properly — not a spoon of straight dressing. Adjust salt and pepper. If it's too sharp add a tiny drizzle more olive oil. If it's too flat add a small splash more vinegar. Get it right before it goes on anything.

5
Store or use immediately

Use it right away or pour it into a jar with a lid. It'll keep in the fridge for up to a week. The oil will solidify slightly when cold — that's normal. Just let it sit at room temp for a few minutes and give it a shake before using.

Quick Info
prep5 min
makes~¾ cup
keeps1 week
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

This goes on everything — salads obviously, but also roasted vegetables, grilled chicken, pasta salad, or as a dipping sauce for bread. Make a double batch. The crew runs through it fast. A mason jar with a lid is the move for storage — shake it before each use.

Crew Tested · Chicken & One Pan

PESTO
CHICKEN
& BROCCOLI

One pan. Twenty minutes. No excuses. Sear the chicken until it has a real crust, steam the vegetables in the same pan, then turn the heat off and let the pesto do the rest. This is the crew's go-to when nobody wants to cook but everybody still needs to eat. Get a good pesto — it carries the whole dish.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 15 min
Serves: 4
Difficulty: Easy
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Tenders
methodOne Pan
total time20 min
difficultyEasy
crew rating8.8 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Chicken breast tenders cut into 1-inch pieces
2 lbs
Sea salt
1 tsp
Cracked black pepper
½ tsp
Garlic powder
1 tbsp
Avocado oil
2 tbsp
The Vegetables
Broccoli cut into small florets
1 head (~1 lb)
Grape tomatoes
10 oz
Chicken broth
½ cup
The Finish
Basil pesto good quality — Costco or Italian imported
2 jars (6.5 oz each)
Parmesan shredded
¼ cup

How We Make It

1
Season the chicken

Slice the chicken tenders into roughly 1-inch pieces and drop them into a bowl. Add the salt, pepper, and garlic powder then toss until every piece is coated. Don't skip the seasoning step — the chicken needs flavor before it hits the pan.

2
Sear hard and don't touch it

Get a large skillet ripping hot over high heat. Add the avocado oil. Once it shimmers, lay the chicken in one even layer. Press it flat. Now leave it alone for 3 minutes. You want a golden-brown crust — that only happens if you stop moving it. Flip once and repeat on the other side.

// High heat, no stirring. That crust is where the flavor lives. A grey steamed piece of chicken is not the same thing.
3
Rest the chicken, deglaze the pan

Pull the chicken out and set it on a plate to rest. Put the same pan back over high heat and pour in the chicken broth. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon — all that brown stuff stuck to the pan is flavor and you want it in the dish. Get it all up.

4
Steam the vegetables

Add the broccoli florets and grape tomatoes straight into the pan with the broth. Put a lid on it and let them steam for 2 minutes — just until the broccoli is barely tender but still has a bite. Don't overcook it. Soft mushy broccoli is not the move.

// Cut the broccoli small so it steams fast and evenly. Big chunks need more time and the tomatoes will turn to mush waiting for them.
5
Turn off the heat and add the pesto

Kill the heat completely. Add the chicken back into the pan then pour in the pesto. Start with one jar, stir everything together, taste it, then add more as needed. The residual heat in the pan is enough — you don't want to cook the pesto or it loses its brightness. Fold until everything is evenly coated.

// Pesto brands vary wildly. Taste as you add. Costco's pesto and Italian imported brands are the crew's picks. Avoid cheap supermarket brands — they taste flat.
6
Finish with Parm and serve

Scatter the shredded Parmesan over the top and bring the whole pan to the table. Serve it family-style straight from the skillet. No plating required. The crew eats this directly out of the pan and calls it done.

Quick Info
prep5 min
cook15 min
serves4
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

Works just as well with chicken thighs, shrimp, or salmon cut into cubes. Swap the broccoli for asparagus, mushrooms, zucchini, or green beans — whatever's in the fridge. For a serious upgrade throw fresh mozzarella on top and hit it with a balsamic drizzle before serving.

Crew Tested · Chicken & Caribbean

JAMAICAN
JERK
CHICKEN

The crew doesn't do bland chicken. This rub has ten spices and every single one of them matters. Get it under the skin, not just on top of it. Bake it hot. The drippings that collect in the pan at the end — that's your sauce. Don't pour them out. Serve this with rice and beans and don't say another word.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Bake: 40-50 min
Serves: 5
Difficulty: Easy
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Legs
methodOven / Bake
bake temp425°F
difficultyEasy
heat levelMedium
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken
Chicken legs
10 pieces
The Jerk Rub
Olive oil binds everything together
⅓ cup
Light brown sugar packed
2 tbsp
Dried thyme
1 tbsp
Ground allspice
2 tsp
Smoked paprika
2 tsp
Cinnamon
¼–½ tsp
Ground ginger
1 tsp
Ground cloves
1 tsp
Cayenne pepper
1 tsp
Garlic powder
1 tsp
Onion powder
1 tsp
Kosher salt
2¼ tsp
Black pepper freshly ground
¼ tsp

How We Make It

1
Build the rub

Preheat the oven to 425°F with the rack on the lower middle position. Combine the olive oil, brown sugar, and every spice in a bowl and mix until it forms a thick paste. Smell it — it should hit immediately. If your spices are old and faint this is the moment you find out. Fresh spices only.

// Mix the dry spices ahead of time and store them in a jar. When you're ready to cook, just add the olive oil and go. The crew keeps a batch ready at all times.
2
Dry the chicken and poke it

Pat every piece of chicken completely dry with paper towels. Moisture is the enemy of a good crust. Then use a fork to poke holes all over each leg — top, bottom, sides. This lets the rub penetrate deeper into the meat instead of just sitting on the surface.

3
Get the rub under the skin

This is the step most people skip and it's the reason their jerk chicken is forgettable. Use your fingers to loosen the skin away from the meat — it peels back easily. Push the rub paste underneath the skin and press it across the whole surface of the meat. Then coat the outside of the skin too. Every surface covered.

// Under the skin is where the flavor actually penetrates. On top of the skin just tastes the surface. Do both.
4
Bake hot with space between pieces

Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil. Place the chicken legs with space between each one — they need airflow to roast, not steam. Slide onto the lower middle rack at 425°F. Smaller legs go 40 minutes, larger legs go 50. You want deep golden brown color on the outside and the skin pulling back slightly at the bone.

5
Serve with the pan drippings

Pull the chicken from the oven and let it rest 5 minutes on the pan. Do not drain or discard the drippings — spoon them over the chicken when you serve. That liquid is concentrated spiced chicken fat and it belongs on the plate. Serve immediately.

// Pair with rice and beans, coconut rice, or plantains. The crew eats this with all three when we're going all in.
Quick Info
prep10 min
bake40–50 min
temp425°F
serves5
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

This is one of the crew's best meal prep recipes. Make a full batch on Sunday and eat it through the week — it reheats well and the flavor actually gets better after a day in the fridge. You can also marinate the raw chicken overnight and bake it the next day. Or freeze it raw with the rub already on and bake straight from thawed.

Crew Tested · Rice & Cuban

CUBAN BLACK
BEANS & RICE

Call it Moros y Cristianos, call it Congri — call it whatever your family called it. The beans and rice cook together, not separate. That's the whole point. The beans stain the rice dark, the bacon fat coats everything, and by the time you lift the lid it smells like something that took all day. It didn't. Don't open that lid until the time is up.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Cook: 50 min
Serves: 4
Difficulty: Easy
Quick Stats
typeRice & Beans
methodStovetop
cuisineCuban
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Base
Thick-cut bacon save every drop of the fat
3 slices
Green bell pepper diced
½ cup
Onion diced
1 small
Garlic cloves minced
2 cloves
Long-grain white rice rinsed
1 cup
Quick Method — Canned Beans
Canned black beans do NOT drain — use the liquid
15 oz can
Water
1 cup
Seasoning
Ground cumin
½ tsp
Dried oregano
½ tsp
Bay leaf
1
Salt & black pepper
to taste

How We Make It

1
Fry the bacon and keep the fat

Lay the bacon slices in a cold Dutch oven or heavy pot and bring it up to medium heat. Let it render slowly until fully cooked and crispy. Pull the bacon out onto a paper towel. Do not touch the fat left in the pot. Do not drain it. Do not wipe it. That fat is the foundation of everything that comes next.

// Thick-cut bacon renders more fat and stays crispier when you stir it back in at the end. Thin bacon works but gives you less of both.
2
Build the sofrito

In the same pot with the bacon fat over medium heat, add the diced green pepper and onion. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until softened. Add the minced garlic and stir for 30 seconds — just until fragrant. Don't let the garlic burn. This is your sofrito base and it sets the flavor for everything else.

3
Add the rice, beans, and liquid

Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir it around in the fat and sofrito for 30 seconds. Then pour in the entire can of black beans — liquid and all. Add the cup of water, cumin, oregano, bay leaf, salt, and pepper. Stir everything once to combine.

// The bean liquid is what turns the rice dark and gives it that deep Cuban flavor. Never drain canned beans for this recipe.
4
Cover and do not open the lid

Bring the pot to a boil, then drop the heat to a low simmer. Put the lid on. Set a timer for 30 minutes. Walk away. The steam is what cooks the rice and makes it fluffy. Every time you lift that lid you lose steam and wreck the texture. Thirty minutes. Lid stays on.

5
Stir and finish

After 30 minutes, lift the lid and give it a good stir from the bottom up so nothing sticks. Cook uncovered for another 5 to 10 minutes until the rice is fully cooked through and the texture is right — fluffy, not wet. Remove from heat, put the lid back on, and let it sit for another 5 minutes.

6
Chop the bacon back in and serve

Roughly chop the crispy bacon you set aside earlier. Fluff the rice and beans with a fork, then fold the bacon pieces through. Taste for salt one more time and adjust. Serve as a side to jerk chicken, roast pork, or anything else the crew is running that night.

// Pairs perfectly with the crew's Jamaican Jerk Chicken. Make both on the same night and eat like you earned it.
Quick Info
prep10 min
cook50 min
serves4
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

This reheats perfectly — add a small splash of water when warming it back up to loosen the rice. Makes great leftovers for 3 to 4 days. If you want it darker use dried beans soaked overnight and cooked in their own liquid — that's the traditional method and the color goes deep. Canned beans are faster but cook lighter.

CABBAGE &
CARROT SLAW

No mayo. No creamy nonsense. Just cabbage, carrots, cider vinegar, and olive oil. This is the slaw you make when you want something that actually tastes like food and doesn't fall apart after an hour on the table. Chill it. It gets better. The crew puts this on everything.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Chill: 1 hr
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
typeSlaw / Side
methodNo Cook
difficultyEasy

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Slaw
Cabbage thinly sliced
2 cups
Carrot strips small, matchstick cut
1 cup
Cider vinegar

Extra virgin olive oil

to taste

How We Make It

1
Slice the cabbage thin

Thin is the move. Thick cabbage chunks stay tough and don't absorb the dressing. Use a sharp knife or a mandoline and get it as fine as you can. Matchstick the carrots to the same size so everything is uniform.

2
Dress and toss

Add the cabbage and carrots to a bowl. Pour over the cider vinegar and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss until everything is evenly coated. Taste it — it should be tangy and lightly dressed, not swimming.

// The vinegar is the whole point. Don't reduce it. It softens the cabbage slightly and gives the slaw its bite.
3
Cover and chill

Cover the bowl and put it in the fridge for at least one hour before serving. The cabbage wilts slightly and absorbs the dressing. This is not optional — a slaw that didn't chill is just raw cabbage with dressing on top.

Crew Tested · Beef & Comfort

PERFECT
POT ROAST

Low and slow is the only way this works. Chuck roast seared hard, braised in red wine and beef broth with rosemary, thyme, and garlic for four hours. You don't check it. You don't rush it. When the fork goes in and the whole thing falls apart — that's when it's done. Make the gravy with the drippings. That's not optional.

⏱ Prep: 25 min
Cook: 4 hrs
300°F
Serves: 8
Quick Stats
proteinChuck Roast
methodOven Braise
oven temp300°F
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Roast
Beef chuck roast or rump roast
3–4 lbs
Olive oil
1 tbsp
Salt & black pepper
generous
The Braise
Yellow onion chopped
1 large
Beef broth
2 cups
Dry red wine cabernet or merlot
1 cup
Garlic cloves coarsely chopped
4 cloves
Dried rosemary
½ tsp
Dried thyme
½ tsp
Bay leaf
1
The Vegetables
Baby potatoes or chopped red potatoes
1 lb
Carrots cut into 2-inch pieces
4
Celery ribs cut into 1½-inch pieces
2
The Gravy
Cornstarch
2 tbsp
Cold water
2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Preheat and season hard

Preheat the oven to 300°F. Season the entire roast — every surface — with a generous amount of salt and black pepper. Don't be shy. This is a big piece of meat and it needs seasoning throughout, not just on top.

2
Sear every side

Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the roast and sear for 4 minutes per side without moving it — top, bottom, and both ends. You want a deep brown crust on every surface. This is what makes the gravy dark and rich. Don't skip the sear.

// If the roast sticks, it's not ready to flip. Wait. It'll release when the crust is properly formed.
3
Build the braise

Arrange the chopped onions around the roast. Combine the beef broth, red wine, garlic, rosemary, and thyme and pour it over and around the meat. Add the bay leaf. Bring it to a simmer on the stovetop, then cover and move the whole pot into the 300°F oven.

4
First 2 hours — meat only

Cook covered for 2 hours. Do not open the oven every 20 minutes. You don't need to check it. The low heat and the lid are doing the work. Leave it alone.

5
Add vegetables for another 2 hours

After 2 hours, pull the pot out and add the potatoes, carrots, and celery around the roast. Cover it back up and put it back in for another 2 hours. For a 3 lb roast, check at 1.5 hours. For a 4+ lb roast, go the full 2. The test is a fork — if it slides in and the meat pulls apart with no resistance, it's done.

6
Make the gravy

Pull the roast and vegetables out of the pot. Discard the bay leaf. Whisk the cornstarch and cold water together until smooth. Bring the remaining liquid to a boil on the stovetop and whisk in the cornstarch slurry a little at a time until the gravy thickens to the right consistency. Taste and season.

// The drippings are already deeply seasoned from 4 hours of braising. Taste before adding any salt.
7
Pull apart and serve

Use two forks to pull the roast into large chunks. Plate the beef and vegetables and spoon the gravy over everything. Serve immediately with bread or mashed potatoes to catch the extra gravy. That's the whole point.

This is a Sunday meal. Plan for it. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge and freeze well for 3 months. The braising liquid freezes too — use it as the base for a beef soup or stew later in the week. No wine? Use all beef broth. It's slightly less complex but still works.

ORANGE
CHICKEN
SAUCE

The crew reverse-engineered this from the takeout box and never looked back. Soy, orange juice, brown sugar, fresh ginger, garlic, sesame oil, and chili flakes. Thickened with cornstarch until it coats everything. Pour it over fried chicken, toss it with rice, use it as a dipping sauce. The orange and ginger hit first. The heat comes after.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 5 min
Makes: ~2 cups
Quick Stats
typeSauce
cuisineAsian-American
makes~2 cups
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce
Soy sauce
3 tbsp
Orange juice
¾ cup
Brown sugar
½ cup
Orange zest
1 orange
Oil
1 tbsp
Ginger root minced
2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Build the slurry first

Whisk the cornstarch and water together in a small bowl until completely smooth with no lumps. Set it aside. If you add dry cornstarch straight to a hot sauce you'll get clumps that never dissolve. Do this step first.

2
Cook the aromatics

Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced ginger and garlic and cook for about 60 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant. Don't let them burn — they go from raw to done to ruined very fast. Watch them.

3
Add the liquids

Pour in the orange juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, orange zest, rice wine, chili flakes, and green onion. Stir everything together and bring it up to a simmer over medium heat. Let it simmer for 2 to 3 minutes so the sugar dissolves and the flavors start to come together.

4
Thicken and finish

Give the cornstarch slurry a quick re-whisk then pour it slowly into the simmering sauce while stirring constantly. The sauce will thicken quickly — keep stirring until it coats the back of a spoon. Pull it off the heat and stir in the sesame oil. That's the sauce.

// The sesame oil goes in at the very end, off the heat. Cooking it kills the flavor. Add it last.

Crew Notes

Toss with crispy fried chicken pieces for classic orange chicken. Also works as a glaze for salmon or shrimp. Keeps in the fridge for a week in a sealed jar — reheat gently on the stove with a splash of water to loosen it back up.

CHICKEN
GYROS

The marinade does the heavy lifting. Olive oil, lemon, garlic, Herbs de Provence — let the chicken sit in it for at least 30 minutes. Two hours if you planned ahead. Cook it hot, slice it thin, and pile everything into a pita. The tzatziki goes on last and it goes on heavy. The crew wraps these tight and eats them fast.

How We Make It

1
Mix the marinade and coat the chicken

Combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, Herbs de Provence, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, salt, and pepper in a bowl and whisk together. Add the chicken tenders, toss until every piece is coated, cover tightly, and refrigerate. Minimum 30 minutes. Two hours is better. Overnight is the crew's move when we plan ahead.

2
Make the cucumber salad

While the chicken marinates, combine the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and dill in a bowl. Toss and set aside. This gets better as it sits — make it first and let it rest while everything else comes together.

3
Cook the chicken hot

Preheat a grill or skillet to medium-high. Use tongs to transfer the chicken — leave the excess marinade behind. Cook 5 to 6 minutes per side until cooked through with good color on the outside. Let it rest for 3 minutes then slice thin against the grain.

// Don't move the chicken constantly. Let it sit and get actual color on each side.
4
Build and wrap

Lay pita flat. Add lettuce, sliced chicken, cucumber salad, feta, and a heavy hand of tzatziki. Fold it over or roll it tight. Eat it immediately — a gyro that sits open on a plate is a tragedy.

Crew Tested · Rice & Bowls

MEDITERRANEAN
YELLOW RICE

Basmati rice toasted in olive oil with onion and garlic, then cooked in stock with turmeric and a cinnamon stick. The color comes from the turmeric. The depth comes from the cinnamon. The crew runs this as the base for shawarma bowls, gyro bowls, and anything else that needs a solid foundation. Rinse the rice. Let it rest after cooking. Use stock not water.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 30 min
Serves: 8
Quick Stats
typeRice / Side
methodStovetop
cuisineMediterranean
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Rice
Basmati rice rinsed until water runs clear
2 cups
Chicken or vegetable stock not water
3 cups
Olive oil
2 tbsp
White onion chopped
1
Garlic cloves minced
2
Turmeric powder
½ tsp
Cinnamon stick
1
Salt & black pepper
1 tsp / ¼ tsp

How We Make It

1
Rinse the rice

Put the basmati in a fine mesh strainer and run cold water over it until the water coming out runs clear. This removes the excess starch that makes rice sticky and gummy. Takes about 2 minutes. Don't skip it.

2
Build the base

Heat olive oil in a wide sauté pan over medium-high heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until golden — not just softened, actually golden. Takes 5 to 7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and stir for about a minute until fragrant. Add the rinsed rice and stir it around in the oil, onion, and garlic for 2 minutes to toast it slightly.

3
Add spices and liquid

Add the turmeric, salt, and pepper and stir to coat the rice evenly. Add the cinnamon stick and pour in the stock. Stir once, bring it to a simmer, and let it cook uncovered until the liquid is almost completely absorbed — about 10 minutes. Watch it.

// Stock over water every time. The stock carries flavor the rice absorbs as it cooks. Plain water gives you plain rice.
4
Cover and finish on low

Once the liquid is almost gone, cover the pan and drop the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 minutes. Don't lift the lid. The steam is finishing the rice and you'll let it out if you peek.

5
Rest and fluff

Turn the heat off completely and leave the lid on for another 10 to 15 minutes. Then fluff with a fork — not a spoon, a fork — and remove the cinnamon stick. Plate it and top with fresh parsley or toasted pine nuts if you have them.

Quick Info
prep5 min
cook30 min
rest10-15 min
serves8
Crew Notes

This is the crew's go-to base for shawarma bowls, gyro bowls, and kebab plates. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat in a pan with a small splash of water and a lid — microwave works but the pan method keeps the texture right. Add peas, raisins, or toasted almonds for variations.

GREEK YOGURT
CHICKEN WRAP

Everything built from scratch — the marinade, the tzatziki, the flatbread. Greek yogurt and spices tenderize the chicken overnight. The flatbread is two ingredients and takes ten minutes. The tzatziki is five minutes. The whole thing comes together faster than you think and tastes like something that took three times as long. The crew builds these and eats them immediately.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Marinate: Overnight
Cook: 15 min
Serves: 2
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Breast
methodPan / Grill
cuisineGreek
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Chicken & Marinade
Chicken breast thinly cut, raw weight
180g
Low fat Greek yogurt
100g
Lemon juice
squeeze
Minced garlic
5g
Salt, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, pepper
to taste
Tzatziki
Low fat Greek yogurt
75g
Minced garlic
5g

handful

to taste

How We Make It

1
Marinate the chicken overnight

Combine the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, minced garlic, and all the spices in a bowl. Add the thinly cut chicken breast and coat everything evenly. Cover and refrigerate overnight. The yogurt tenderizes the meat and the spices go deep. Same-day marinating works — minimum 30 minutes — but overnight is the crew's standard.

2
Make the tzatziki

Grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much water as you can with your hands or a clean cloth. Mix it with the Greek yogurt, minced garlic, dill, salt, and a squeeze of lemon. Taste and adjust. Refrigerate until you need it — it gets better as it sits.

// Squeeze the cucumber hard. Excess water makes the tzatziki watery and it won't cling to the wrap properly.
3
Make the flatbread

Mix the flour and Greek yogurt together until a dough forms. It'll be slightly sticky — that's right. Turn it out, shape it into a flat round, and cook in a dry non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred spots appear and it's cooked through. Scatter parsley flakes on top if using.

4
Cook the chicken

Heat a pan or grill to medium-high. Cook the marinated chicken for 4 to 5 minutes per side until fully cooked through with good color. Slice thin after resting for 2 minutes.

5
Build and wrap

Lay the warm flatbread out. Add sliced tomato, red onion, the chicken, and spoon the tzatziki over everything. Add fresh parsley if using. Wrap it, hold it tight, and eat it immediately while the bread is still warm.

prep20 min
marinateovernight

serves2
Crew Notes

The flatbread is a two-ingredient recipe and it slaps. Scale the chicken up and batch-cook it for the week — it stays good in the fridge for 3 days and works in bowls, wraps, or straight off the plate. The tzatziki is also good as a dipping sauce for vegetables or pita chips.

Crew Tested · Beef & Burgers

SMASH
BURGER

80/20. No exceptions. 3oz balls, screaming hot griddle, smash them flat and don't touch them again. The crust forms in that first minute and that's what makes a smash burger a smash burger. The sauce has mayo, mustard, hot sauce, and Worcestershire mixed right in. American cheese on top while it's still on the heat. Eat it immediately.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Cook: 5 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
protein80/20 Beef
patty size3 oz each
methodGriddle / Cast Iron
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Burger
Ground beef 80/20, Certified Angus if you can get it
1½ lbs
Kosher salt
1½ tsp
Black pepper
½ tsp
American cheese slices
4 slices
White hamburger buns toasted in butter
4
The Sauce
Mayonnaise
½ cup
Yellow mustard
1 tbsp
Grated yellow onion
1 tbsp
Hot sauce
2 tsp
Worcestershire sauce
1 tsp
Butter room temp, for buns
2 tbsp
Toppings
Shredded iceberg lettuce
2 cups
Vine-ripe tomatoes sliced
8 slices

How We Make It

1
Make the sauce

Mix mayo, mustard, grated onion, hot sauce, and Worcestershire together until combined. Taste it. Adjust. Set aside. This is the move that separates a smash burger from a regular burger — don't skip the sauce.

2
Ball up the beef — 3oz each

Divide the ground beef into 3oz balls. Do not season yet and do not overwork the meat — just roll them loosely. Overworked beef makes dense patties. You want loose, shaggy balls that smash open and create craggy edges. Those edges are where the crust forms.

// 3oz per ball. Not more. The smash needs room to spread and thin enough to get that full crust.
3
Get the griddle screaming hot

A cast iron griddle or skillet over high heat for at least 3 minutes until ripping hot. You want smoke. If you're not getting any smoke the surface isn't hot enough and you'll steam the burger instead of searing it.

4
Smash and don't touch

Place a beef ball on the hot surface. Season with salt and pepper immediately. Place a piece of parchment over the top and smash it flat with a heavy spatula — press hard and hold for 10 seconds. Season the top. Now leave it. Don't touch it. Don't move it. Let it cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges turn brown and the top is mostly grey.

// The crust only forms if you leave it alone. Every time you move it you break the sear.
5
Flip once, cheese immediately

Flip with a thin spatula — scrape under it hard to get the crust. Lay American cheese on top immediately. Cook for 45 seconds to 1 minute more. That's it. Pull it.

6
Toast the buns and build

Butter the cut sides of each bun and toast face-down on the same griddle until golden. Spread sauce on both halves. Bottom bun, lettuce, tomato, patty with melted cheese, top bun. Eat it immediately. A smash burger that sits gets soggy. Don't let it sit.

Quick Info
prep10 min
cook5 min
serves4
patty size3 oz
Crew Notes

80/20 is non-negotiable. The fat is what creates the crust and keeps it juicy. Leaner beef makes a dry, flat, sad smash burger. Don't do it. Double patties are always valid — stack two 3oz patties with a cheese slice between them for the proper double smash.

Crew Tested · Baking & Bread

HOMEMADE
PITA BREAD

The crew makes this for gyros, shawarma, and anything else that needs something to hold it. Six ingredients, one hour rise, two minutes in a screaming hot cast iron. They puff up and pocket right in front of you. Cover them immediately with a towel after pulling them out — the steam keeps them soft. Store-bought pita is fine. This is something else.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Rise: 1 hr
Cook: 3 min each
Makes: 8
Quick Stats
typeFlatbread
methodCast Iron / Oven
makes8 pitas
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Lukewarm water
1 cup
Active dry yeast
2 tsp
Sugar
½ tsp
All-purpose flour divided
3 cups
Kosher salt
1–2 tsp
Extra virgin olive oil plus more for the bowl
2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Proof the yeast

Combine lukewarm water, yeast, and sugar in a large bowl. Stir until dissolved. Add ½ cup flour and whisk together. Leave it uncovered in a warm spot for 15 minutes. It should be frothy and bubbly. If it's flat and dead your yeast is done — start over with fresh yeast.

2
Form and knead the dough

Add salt, olive oil, and most of the remaining flour (keep ½ cup for dusting). Stir until the dough comes together in a shaggy mass. Dust with a little flour and knead inside the bowl for 1 minute. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Rest 10 minutes, then knead again for 2 more minutes. The dough should be soft and slightly tacky — not dry.

// Don't overflour. A slightly tacky dough makes a better pita than a stiff dry one.
3
Rise for 1 hour

Oil a clean bowl lightly and place the dough inside, turning it to coat. Cover tightly with plastic wrap then a kitchen towel. Leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour until doubled in size.

4
Divide and rest

Deflate the dough gently and divide into 7 to 8 equal balls. Cover with a towel and let them rest for 10 minutes. This rest makes them easier to roll out without snapping back.

5
Roll thin and cook hot

Roll each ball into an 8 to 9 inch circle about ¼ inch thick. Cook in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat with just a tiny wipe of olive oil. Cook 30 seconds until bubbles form, flip, cook 1 to 2 minutes until toasted spots appear underneath, flip again and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. It's done when it puffs and forms a pocket.

// Cover finished pitas immediately with a clean towel. The trapped steam keeps them soft and pliable. Uncovered pitas go stiff.
Quick Info
prep15 min
rise1 hr
cook3 min each
makes8
Crew Notes

Store baked pitas in an airtight bag for a few days or freeze for up to 3 months — reheat from frozen in a medium oven, no thawing needed. The dough can also be made ahead and kept in the fridge up to a week, then bake as many as you need at a time.

Crew Favorite · Pork & Mexican

CARNITAS

The crew's personal favorite recipe on this entire site. Lard — not Crisco, not vegetable oil, lard. Pork chunks browned hard in batches, pressure cooked with Coke, two whole oranges, two limes, a lot of garlic, and bay leaf for an hour. Then the meat goes on a tray, gets hit with the braising liquid, and goes under the broiler until the edges shatter. That's carnitas. Everything else is pork.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Pressure Cook: 1 hr
Broil: 5-10 min
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
proteinPork Shoulder
methodPressure Cook + Broil
difficultyMedium
crew rating10 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Pork
Pork shoulder cut into large chunks
3–4 lbs
Lard not Crisco — real lard
generous amount
Garlic cloves lots of them
8–10 cloves
White onion diced
½
Coke or Pepsi glass bottle preferred
1 bottle
Oranges juice of 2, peel of 1
2
Limes juice and peel of 1–2
1–2
Bay leaf
1–2
The Seasoning
Garlic powder
generous
Onion powder
generous
Cumin
generous
Dried oregano
generous
Dried thyme
generous
Salt & black pepper
generous

How We Make It

1
Brown the pork in lard — don't overcrowd

Heat a generous amount of lard in a heavy pot or the pressure cooker insert over high heat. Season the pork chunks heavily with all the dry spices. Brown in batches — never overcrowd the pan. Each piece needs actual contact with the hot surface to form a crust. Brown on all sides, pulling each batch out before adding the next. This step takes time. Don't rush it.

// Overcrowding drops the temperature and you steam the pork instead of searing it. Brown in batches every time.
2
Add everything and pressure cook

Return all the browned pork to the pressure cooker. Add the diced onion, whole garlic cloves, Coke, orange juice, orange peel, lime juice, lime peel, and bay leaves. Pressure cook on high for 1 hour. The liquid should cover at least halfway up the pork — add water if needed.

3
Transfer to tray and broil

Transfer the cooked pork to a rimmed baking sheet. Spoon some of the braising liquid over the top — enough to coat it but not drown it. Set the broiler to high. Broil for 5 to 10 minutes until the edges are deeply browned and crisping up. Watch it closely — it goes from crispy to burnt fast. Pull it the moment you see the edges shattering.

// The braising liquid caramelizes on the outside of the meat under the broiler. That's what creates the crispy bits. Those bits are the whole point.
4
Pull and serve

Use two forks to pull the carnitas apart — it should shred effortlessly. Serve in warm tortillas with whatever the crew has going — salsa, guacamole, pickled red onion, or just lime and cilantro. The crew doesn't complicate it.

Quick Info
prep20 min
pressure cook1 hr
broil5-10 min
serves6
Crew Notes

This is the crew's personal favorite. Make a big batch — carnitas reheats perfectly in a hot skillet with a little of the reserved braising liquid. The leftover liquid freezes well and can be used as a base for soups. Glass bottle Coke is the move — canned works but the glass bottle version has more flavor.

MEXICAN
BOWL

Every component built from scratch. Cilantro lime rice, chipotle chicken thighs, charred corn relish, pickled red onions, seasoned black beans, and a spicy garlic mayo that ties everything together. This one takes time and it's worth every minute. The crew builds this when we mean business.

⏱ Active: 60 min
Serves: 6
Medium
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
components5
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Cilantro Lime Rice
White rice
3 cups / 600g
Water
3 cups / 709ml

2 tbsp

1
Cilantro finely chopped

to taste

4 cloves

½

to taste
Pickled Red Onion

1 cup

1 cup

1 tbsp

½

2 cans
White onion diced

Serrano diced
1

4 cloves

Mayonnaise

8 cloves

How We Make It

1
Start the pickled onions first

Bring vinegar, water, and salt to a simmer and stir until salt dissolves. Pour over thinly sliced red onion in a jar. Cool at room temp then refrigerate. They're ready in 30 minutes and better after a few hours. The crew always has these in the fridge.

2
Make the spicy garlic mayo

Mix grated garlic, hot sauce, onion powder, salt, and pepper into the mayo. Taste and adjust heat. Refrigerate until serving. This sauce carries the whole bowl — don't be shy with the garlic.

3
Season and cook the chicken

Mix the finely chopped chipotle peppers, garlic, and salt together and coat the chicken thighs thoroughly. Cook in a greased grill pan or cast iron over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes then slice thin.

// The whole can of chipotles makes it seriously spicy. Use half if you want it manageable. The crew uses the whole can.
4
Cook the rice

Combine rice and water in a pot, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, cover and cook until water is absorbed — about 18 minutes. Fluff with a fork and fold in butter, lime juice, lime zest, cilantro, and salt while still hot. Taste and adjust.

5
Char the corn relish

Grill or char the corn directly over a flame or in a cast iron until kernels are deeply browned in spots. Cut the kernels off the cob. Char the jalapeños the same way, then finely dice. Mix corn, jalapeños, diced red onion, cilantro, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Set aside.

6
Build the black beans

Heat oil in a saucepan. Cook onion and serrano for 5 minutes until soft. Add tomato and cook 3 minutes. Pour in the beans and chicken stock. Simmer 10 minutes. Add the garlic at the very end, stir for 1 minute, then season. The garlic goes in last so it stays bright and sharp.

7
Build the bowl

Rice on the bottom. Chicken on top. Corn relish, black beans, and pickled red onions alongside. Drizzle the spicy garlic mayo generously over everything. Eat immediately while the rice is still hot.

Quick Info
active time~60 min
serves6
difficultymedium
Crew Notes

The crew batch cooks every component separately and stores them in the fridge. Individual servings all week. Each element keeps 4 to 5 days. The pickled onions improve every day. The spicy garlic mayo keeps a week and goes on everything — tacos, sandwiches, eggs, anything.

BLACK PEPPER
CHICKEN

The crew ran the takeout box version for years before figuring this out. The key is pulling the chicken out of the pan before it's done, charring the vegetables separately, then bringing it all back together in a black pepper sauce that thickens in seconds. Each element cooked right. Not steamed, not overcooked. Everything gets its moment in the pan.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Cook: 5 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Breast
methodStir Fry
total time25 min
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Chicken & Marinade
Chicken breast or thighs sliced against grain ¼" thick
1 lb
Light soy sauce
1 tbsp
Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
1 tbsp
Cornstarch
1 tbsp
Black Pepper Sauce
Chicken broth
½ cup
Light soy sauce
2 tbsp
Shaoxing wine
2 tbsp
Dark soy sauce
2 tsp
Cornstarch
1 tbsp
Sugar
1½ tbsp
Coarsely ground black pepper
2 tsp
Salt
⅛ tsp
Stir Fry
Peanut or vegetable oil
2 tbsp
Ginger minced
1 tbsp
Garlic minced
2 cloves
White onion chopped
½
Bell peppers mixed colors, chopped
2

How We Make It

1
Marinate the chicken

Combine the sliced chicken with soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and cornstarch. Toss until every piece is coated with a thin layer. Marinate for 10 to 15 minutes. The cornstarch is what keeps the chicken juicy under high heat — it creates a protective coating around the meat.

2
Mix the sauce

Combine all sauce ingredients in a small bowl and mix well. The cornstarch will settle to the bottom — give it a stir right before you add it to the pan.

3
Sear the chicken and pull it out

Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large skillet over medium-high until hot. Spread the chicken in a single layer with as little overlap as possible. Sear for 1 minute without touching it. Flip and cook 30 seconds more until browned but still slightly pink inside. Pull it out and set aside. It finishes in the sauce.

// Pulling the chicken out before it's done is not optional. If you leave it in, it overcooks while the vegetables cook and turns dry and chewy.
4
Char the vegetables

Add the remaining oil to the pan. Add ginger and garlic — quick stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the onion and bell peppers and stir-fry for 20 seconds. You want them to stay crisp with some color — not soft.

5
Sauce, chicken back in, done

Stir the sauce mixture one more time and pour it into the pan. It will thicken fast — stir immediately. Once it coats the back of a spoon, add the chicken back in and toss everything together for a few seconds. Pull the pan off the heat immediately and transfer to a plate. The carry-over heat will keep cooking it if you leave it in the pan.

cook5 min
serves4
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

Have everything cut and measured before you start cooking — this dish moves fast. The active cook time is under 5 minutes. Swap bell pepper for asparagus, cabbage, or broccoli. Works with chicken thighs too. Serve over steamed white rice.

Crew Tested · Breakfast & Baking

FLUFFY
PANCAKES

No buttermilk. No special equipment. Eight ingredients, one bowl, don't overmix. The batter is thicker than you expect and that's right — it's what makes them tall. Medium heat, wait for the bubbles and defined edges before flipping, don't press down on the spatula after you flip. The crew makes these on weekends and sometimes Tuesday.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 10 min
Makes: 8
Quick Stats
typeBreakfast
makes8 pancakes
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Batter
All-purpose flour
1½ cups
Baking powder aluminum-free if you have it
2½ tsp
Salt
½ tsp
Sugar
2 tbsp
Milk any kind
1¼ cups
Egg
1
Butter melted
3 tbsp
Vanilla extract
2 tsp

How We Make It

1
Combine dry ingredients

Mix flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar together in a large bowl. Make a well in the center — push the dry ingredients to the sides to create a clear space in the middle. This is where the wet ingredients go.

2
Add wet and mix until just combined

Pour the milk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla into the well. Break up the egg with a fork first, then mix everything together working from the outside in. Stop the moment you no longer see dry flour — lumps are fine, lumps are good. Overmixing develops gluten and makes chewy, flat pancakes. Mix less than you think you need to.

// The batter should be thick and scoopable, not runny. If it pours like water something went wrong. It won't self-level in the pan — use the back of your scoop to shape it slightly.
3
Cook on medium — not high

Heat a non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Grease with butter or cooking spray. Pour ¼ cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look set and defined — about 2 minutes. Flip once and cook 1 to 1.5 minutes more. Do not press down with the spatula after flipping. That squeezes out the air bubbles and collapses the fluff.

4
Keep warm and serve

Keep finished pancakes warm on a sheet pan in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest. Stack them, butter them while hot, and hit them with warm syrup. The crew doesn't wait for the whole batch — we eat as they come off the pan.

Quick Info
prep5 min
cook10 min
makes8
difficultyeasy
Crew Notes

Make the batter the night before and refrigerate — let it come to room temp for 20 minutes before cooking. Leftover pancakes freeze well for up to 3 months and reheat in the toaster. Fold in blueberries or chocolate chips right before cooking for variations.

GARLIC
NAAN

The crew runs these alongside curry, grilled chicken, dips, and anything else that needs something to soak it up. Let the dough rest 30 minutes, roll it thin, grill it until it puffs and chars. The garlic butter goes on immediately after pulling it off the heat so it soaks straight in. Best eaten hot off the grill. Don't let them sit.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Rest: 30 min
Cook: 5 min each
Makes: 4
Quick Stats
typeFlatbread
methodGrill / Cast Iron
makes4 naans
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dough
Plain flour
250g
Baking powder
½ tsp
Salt
1 tsp
Sugar
1 tsp
Active dry yeast
1 tsp
Warm milk
120ml
Vegetable oil
2 tbsp
Garlic Butter
Garlic cloves minced
2
Fresh coriander chopped
2 tbsp
Butter melted
2 tbsp

How We Make It

1
Mix and knead the dough

Whisk together flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, and yeast in a large bowl. Add warm milk in small increments and the vegetable oil, mixing as you go until a soft dough forms. Knead for a few minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic — it shouldn't stick to your hands.

2
Rest 30 minutes

Cover the dough with a damp cloth and leave it in a warm spot for 30 minutes. It won't rise dramatically like a yeasted bread — that's fine. The rest lets the gluten relax so you can roll it thin without it springing back.

3
Make the garlic butter

Mix the minced garlic, chopped coriander, and melted butter together in a small bowl. Set it near the grill so you can brush it on immediately when each naan comes off.

4
Roll thin and grill

Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces. Roll each one into a thin circle — thinner than you think, about ⅛ inch. Preheat your grill or cast iron to high. Brush the garlic butter on one side of each naan and place buttered side down on the hot surface. Cook 2 to 3 minutes until the naan starts to puff and get golden marks. Flip and cook another 1 to 2 minutes on the other side.

// High heat and thin dough is what creates the char and puff. Medium heat gives you pale, flat, sad naan.
5
Brush and serve immediately

Pull the naan off the heat and brush any remaining garlic butter over the top immediately while it's hot. The heat draws the butter and garlic into the bread. Serve right away.

Quick Info
prep10 min
rest30 min
cook5 min each
makes4
Crew Notes

Naan is best fresh off the grill. If you need to make ahead, stack them and wrap in foil — reheat in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side. The crew uses these to scoop up curries, stews, and dips. Also pairs well with the crew's Jamaican Jerk Chicken.

LEMONGRASS
BEEF
STIR-FRY

Skirt steak sliced against the grain, marinated in lemongrass, soy, brown sugar, chili oil, ginger, and cornstarch. The cornstarch is the velveting technique — it coats the beef and keeps it juicy under high heat. Charred hard in a wok with snow peas and bell pepper. Sweet, spicy, and fragrant. Better than anything that comes in a box.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Marinate: 15 min
Cook: 30 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinSkirt Steak
methodWok / Stir Fry
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Beef & Marinade
Skirt steak or flank steak
16 oz
Lemongrass paste
1 tbsp
Ginger minced
2 tsp
Garlic minced
1 tsp
Brown sugar
2 tbsp
Light soy sauce
4 tbsp
Red Fresno chili minced — or serrano
1
Chili oil
1 tsp
Rice vinegar
1 tsp
Cornstarch
2 tsp
Stir Fry
Neutral oil divided

Yellow onion halved and thinly sliced
1
Snow peas strings removed

Red bell pepper sliced

How We Make It

1
Build the marinade and slice the beef

Combine all marinade ingredients except cornstarch in a large bowl and mix well. Taste and adjust. Add cornstarch and stir until smooth. Cut the steak with the grain into 4-inch sections, then slice each section against the grain into ½-inch strips. This two-step cut gives you the most tender result. Add the beef to the marinade and refrigerate for 15 minutes.

// Always cut steak against the grain for stir fry. With the grain gives you tough, chewy strips. Against it gives you tender pieces that fall apart right.
2
Char the vegetables hard

Heat half the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the onion, snow peas, and bell pepper. Cook in batches if needed — don't overcrowd. Toss occasionally until the pepper gets char spots and the snow peas are bright green and just tender, about 5 to 7 minutes. Add ginger, stir 1 minute. Season with salt and pepper. Remove to a bowl.

3
Cook the beef hot and fast

Add remaining oil to the pan over medium-high heat. Pour in the beef with all of the marinade. Spread into an even layer. Cook 3 to 4 minutes — crank the heat in the first 3 minutes to develop a sear without burning. It will look like the sauce separates as it cooks. That's normal. Flip the beef and continue cooking, turning occasionally, 2 to 4 minutes until mostly cooked through.

4
Water, sauce, vegetables back in

Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and stir — the liquid will tighten into a thick glossy sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning. Turn off the heat, stir in the vegetables, and toss everything to coat. Serve immediately over white rice with cilantro, scallions, lime wedges, and crispy shallots.

serves4
Crew Notes

No lemongrass paste? Use finely minced fresh lemongrass — just the lower pale part of the stalk. Swap the steak for chicken strips or shrimp. Asparagus, bok choy, or broccoli all work instead of snow peas. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

Crew Tested · Sides & Extras

CRISPY
ROAST
POTATOES

The move that makes these is the shake. Parboil until just barely soft, drain, then shake the pot hard until the edges rough up and go fluffy. That roughed-up surface is what goes golden and shatters in the oven. Olive oil, rosemary, salt, pepper, 400°F for 45 minutes. The crew runs these alongside the pot roast and jerk chicken. Simple and right.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Cook: 50 min
400°F
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
typeSide Dish
methodBoil + Roast
oven temp400°F
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Potatoes
Potatoes peeled and cut into chunks
1 kg (~2.2 lbs)
Olive oil
50ml (~3.5 tbsp)
Fresh rosemary sprigs
2–3
Salt & black pepper
generous

How We Make It

1
Preheat and salt the water

Preheat the oven to 400°F. Place the potato chunks in a large pot of cold, well-salted water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the outside is just starting to soften but the inside isn't cooked through. They should be slightly underdone — they finish in the oven.

2
The shake — don't skip this

Drain the potatoes and return them to the empty pot. Put the lid on and shake the pot hard for 10 to 15 seconds. The edges will rough up and turn fluffy. Those rough, fluffy edges are what go crispy in the oven. Alternatively, use a colander and shake it. Either way — shake them until they look roughed up.

// This is the step. Smooth potato edges make smooth roasted potatoes. Rough edges make the shattered, golden, crispy crust. Don't skip the shake.
3
Oil, season, and roast

Transfer the potatoes carefully to a large roasting tin. Drizzle the olive oil over them and season generously with salt and pepper. Add the rosemary sprigs. Toss everything together so every potato is coated. Spread them out in a single layer — crowded potatoes steam instead of roast.

4
Roast 40–45 minutes, turn twice

Roast at 400°F for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once or twice during cooking so they get golden on all sides. They're done when deeply golden brown and the outside shatters slightly when you press one with a spoon. Serve hot. They go soft if they sit.

Quick Info
prep10 min
boil10 min
roast40-45 min
serves6
Crew Notes

The crew uses Yukon Gold or Maris Piper — they have the right starch content for crispy outsides and fluffy insides. Russets work but go fluffier inside. Waxy potatoes like red potatoes won't crisp the same way. Serve immediately — these are best the second they come out of the oven.

MEXICAN
BLACK
BEANS

Two cans of black beans — undrained. That liquid is starch and flavor, don't pour it out. Onion and garlic softened in oil, cumin and cayenne bloomed for a minute, beans poured in and simmered until the liquid thickens into a sauce. Twenty minutes. Better than the side order at any restaurant. The crew finishes these with fresh cilantro every time.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 15 min
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
typeBeans / Side
methodStovetop
difficultyEasy
crew rating8.8 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Beans
Vegetable oil
1 tbsp
Small yellow onion diced

How We Make It

1
Sweat the onion

Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and translucent. Don't rush this step — a properly softened onion builds the base for the whole dish.

2
Bloom the spices

Stir in the minced garlic, cumin, and cayenne. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly. This brief bloom in hot oil activates the spices and deepens the flavor considerably.

3
Add beans — liquid included

Pour in both cans of black beans, liquid and all. Stir to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, letting the liquid reduce slightly and thicken. Season with salt to taste.

// For true restaurant style: stir in 2-3 tbsp of butter or lard at this point and let it melt in. Richer beans, deeper color, better texture.
4
Finish and serve

Top with fresh cilantro and serve hot. These pair with everything Mexican in the vault — carnitas, enchiladas, carne asada, Mexican bowl, and burritos.

prep5 min
cook15 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months. Flavors improve overnight. Smash them with a potato masher for a rustic refried-style version — add water a tablespoon at a time to loosen if needed.

CHIPOTLE
BLACK
BEANS

The crew cracked why Chipotle's beans taste different from every other black bean recipe — they finish with both lemon AND lime juice. The double citrus hit is what makes it. Drain and rinse the cans, build a spiced base, simmer with water until thickened, finish with citrus. Tastes like you ordered it through the app without the markup.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Cook: 15 min
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
typeBeans / Copycat
methodStovetop
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Beans
Oil
1 tbsp
Onion diced
1 small
Garlic minced
6 cloves
Bay leaf
1
Cumin
½ tbsp
Chili powder
1 tbsp
Cayenne pepper
½ tsp

Black beans canned, drained and rinsed
2 cans (~19 oz each)

Lime juice fresh
1 lime
Lemon juice fresh

How We Make It

1
Drain and rinse the beans

Empty both cans into a strainer and rinse under cold water until the water runs clear. This removes the canning liquid (salty, starchy, not the flavor you want) so the beans absorb the sauce you build instead.

2
Build the spiced base

Heat oil in a medium pan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 1 to 2 minutes until translucent. Add minced garlic and cook another minute. Add the bay leaf, cumin, chili powder, cayenne, smoked paprika, and salt. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is fragrant and deeply colored.

3
Simmer until thickened

Add the rinsed beans and 1 cup of water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has reduced into a thick sauce that coats the beans. Don't rush — let it go a full 15 for a deeper color and more concentrated flavor.

// The longer these simmer, the better they get. The 10-minute version is fine. The 15-minute version is what you came for.
4
Finish with lemon AND lime

Squeeze in the juice of one lime and one lemon. Stir to combine. Taste and adjust salt if needed. This double-citrus finish is the Chipotle secret — don't use just one or the other.

Quick Info
prep5 min
cook15 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Keeps 5 days refrigerated, freezes for 6 months. Tastes even better the next day. The crew doubles this and runs it through the whole week — burrito bowls, taco nights, Mexican bowls, eggs. Serve with fresh cilantro and lime wedges.

Crew Tested · Noodles & Thai

PAD THAI

The crew's version. Fresh Thai rice noodles, 2 pounds of chicken sliced thin, eggs scrambled right in the wok, roasted peppers charred separately, tamarind-fish-oyster sauce poured over everything at the end. Crushed peanuts on top. Bean sprouts, green onion, shredded carrot. Wok has to be screaming hot. Everything moves fast.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Cook: 20 min
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
proteinChicken
methodWok / High Heat
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce (mix first)
Tamarind concentrate
2 tbsp
Brown sugar packed
6 tbsp
Fish sauce
¼ cup
Oyster sauce
3 tbsp
The Wok
Fresh Thai-style rice noodles
16 oz bag
Chicken sliced thin, salted
2 lbs
Eggs
6
Garlic cloves minced
5
Onion
1
Red peppers
2
Bean sprouts
2 cups
Green onion
½ cup
Chicken broth if noodles are too dry
up to 1½ cups
To Finish
Crushed peanuts roasted first if possible
generous
Red chili flakes
to taste
Shredded carrots
handful
Edamame optional
optional

How We Make It

1
Mix the sauce first

Combine tamarind concentrate, brown sugar, fish sauce, and oyster sauce in a bowl. Mix until the sugar dissolves. Taste it — it should be sweet, sour, salty, and funky all at once. This goes in near the end, so have it ready.

2
Roast the peppers, set aside

Char the red peppers directly over a flame or in a dry screaming hot cast iron until blistered all over. Pull them off, let them steam in a covered bowl for a few minutes, then peel and slice. Set aside. This step adds a depth that raw pepper can't.

3
Optional: roast the peanuts

Toss peanuts in a dry pan over medium heat, shaking constantly, until golden and fragrant — about 3 to 4 minutes. Pull off immediately and let cool. Crush roughly. Set aside.

4
Cook the onion, garlic, and chicken

Get the wok screaming hot. Add oil and cook onion and garlic for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the salted, thinly sliced chicken and cook until just done through — don't overcrowd. Work in batches if needed.

5
Add noodles

Add the fresh rice noodles directly to the wok with the chicken. Toss everything together over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. If the noodles feel stiff or start clumping, add a splash of chicken broth — just enough to loosen, not drown.

6
Make space and cook the eggs

Push the noodles and chicken to one side of the wok. Crack in all 6 eggs and scramble them in the open space — let them just barely set before folding them into the noodles.

7
Pour in sauce, mix, taste

Pour the sauce evenly over everything. Toss hard to coat every noodle. Taste immediately — adjust with a splash more fish sauce for salt, sugar for sweetness, or tamarind for sourness. Add more broth if noodles are still stiff.

8
Finish and plate

Fold in the roasted peppers and half the peanuts. Transfer to plates. Top with bean sprouts, green onion, shredded carrots, remaining peanuts, and red chili flakes. Serve immediately while hot.

Quick Info
prep20 min
cook20 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Everything has to be prepped before the wok goes on. This moves fast once the heat is on. Tamarind concentrate is in the international or Asian aisle — don't sub anything else, it's the backbone of the dish. Fresh noodles only for this one.
