Crew Tested · Noodles & Chinese

PANDA EXPRESS
CHOW MEIN

The crew's version of the orange box side that disappears before every other dish on the table. Fresh yakisoba noodles rinsed and ready, onion and celery sautéed until soft, cabbage in for a minute, then noodles and the sauce over high heat for 3 minutes. Total cook time is 5 minutes. The prep takes longer. Have everything ready before the pan goes on.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Cook: 5 min
Serves: 8
Quick Stats
typeNoodles / Side
methodWok / Stir Fry
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce
Soy sauce
¼ cup
Brown sugar
1 tbsp
Garlic minced
2 cloves
Fresh ginger grated
1 tsp
Black pepper
to taste
The Noodles & Veg
Yakisoba noodles refrigerated, discard flavor packets, rinse cold
3 packs (17 oz total)
Vegetable oil
2-3 tbsp
White or yellow onion thinly sliced
1 medium
Celery sliced diagonally
⅔ cup
Green cabbage chopped
2 cups

How We Make It

1
Mix the sauce

Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and black pepper together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Set it next to the stove — this goes in fast once cooking starts.

2
Prep the noodles

Open the yakisoba packs and throw out the included flavor packets — you don't need them. Rinse the noodles well in cold water, separating them as you go, then drain thoroughly. Set aside.

// These noodles come from the refrigerated produce section — already soft. Do NOT use dry noodles from the pantry aisle without cooking them first.
3
Sauté the vegetables

Heat oil in a large wok or deep skillet over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and celery and sauté for 1 to 2 minutes until the onion starts to soften. Add the cabbage and cook for 1 more minute, stirring constantly. You want the vegetables tender but still with some bite — not limp.

4
Add noodles and sauce, stir fry

Add the drained noodles and pour the sauce over everything. Crank the heat to medium-high. Stir fry constantly for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are heated through and every strand is coated in the sauce. Serve immediately.

// Don't overcook. The noodles only need heat, not more cooking. 3 minutes max or they start breaking apart.
Quick Info
prep20 min
cook5 min
serves8
Crew Notes

Add cooked chicken, beef, or shrimp to turn this into a full meal. Add a small drizzle of sesame oil at the end for depth — use it sparingly, it overpowers fast. Keeps 4-5 days in the fridge; reheat with a splash of water or soy sauce.

Crew Tested · Sauce & Italian

SIMPLE
ALFREDO
SAUCE

Butter, one big crushed garlic clove, a full 16oz carton of whipping cream reduced for 25 minutes, finely grated parmesan stirred in at the end. Four ingredients. No jar. No shortcuts. The reduction is what makes it — don't rush the 20 to 30 minutes of gentle simmering. What comes out the other side coats pasta like nothing from a store shelf.

⏱ Prep: 2 min
Cook: 30 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
typeSauce
methodStovetop
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce
Butter
2 tbsp
Large garlic clove crushed
1 big one
Heavy whipping cream
16 oz carton
Parmesan cheese finely grated
½ cup
Kosher salt
large pinch
Freshly ground black pepper
3-4 grinds

How We Make It

1
Start low with butter and garlic

Heat the butter in a large deep skillet over low to medium heat. Add the crushed garlic clove and cook for 1 minute — don't let it brown, just soften and infuse the butter. One whole crushed clove is the move, not minced — it gives flavor without turning acrid.

2
Add cream and reduce — 20 to 30 minutes

Pour the full carton of whipping cream into the pan. Stir to combine with the garlic butter. Cook at a low steady simmer for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. The cream will slowly reduce and thicken — you're looking for a sauce that coats the back of a spoon and has reduced by about a third. Don't crank the heat to speed it up; that breaks the sauce.

// This step cannot be rushed. The reduction is what makes it Alfredo and not just cream with cheese. Low and slow, 20-30 minutes minimum.
3
Add parmesan and finish

Add the finely grated parmesan and stir continuously for 3 to 4 minutes until fully melted and incorporated. Season with salt and fresh black pepper. The sauce is done when it's thick, glossy, and coats a spoon without dripping off.

4
Pour over pasta and eat immediately

Toss with your pasta of choice — fettuccine is classic, but the crew puts this on penne, rigatoni, and whatever else is in the cabinet. Add cooked chicken, shrimp, bacon, or mushrooms. Eat it while it's hot — Alfredo seizes up as it cools.

Quick Info
prep2 min
reduce20-30 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Grate the parmesan fresh — pre-grated bagged parmesan has anti-caking agents that make the sauce gritty instead of smooth. A microplane makes fast work of it. Leftovers reheat gently in a pan with a splash of pasta water or cream to loosen.

Crew Tested · Korean & Bowl

KOREAN
PORK
BOWL

The crew combined two recipes into one bowl that earns its real estate in the rotation. Korean-style pork braised slow with soy, gochujang, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger — then a second layer of spicy stir-fried pork with chili paste and sesame. Both piled over steamed white rice. The sweet-spicy-savory thing Cupbop built their whole brand around — done at home.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Cook: 4-6 hrs slow or 30 min fast
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
proteinPork
methodSlow Cooker or Stovetop
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Slow Cooker Korean Pork (Cupbop-style)
Boneless pork shoulder or butt
2-3 lbs
Soy sauce
¼ cup
Brown sugar
3 tbsp
Gochujang Korean chili paste
2-3 tbsp
Garlic minced
5 cloves
Fresh ginger grated
1 tbsp
Sesame oil
1 tsp
Rice vinegar
1 tbsp
Spicy Korean Stir-Fry Pork
Pork belly or shoulder thinly sliced
1 lb
Gochujang
2 tbsp
Soy sauce
1 tbsp
Brown sugar
1 tbsp
Garlic minced
3 cloves
Sesame oil
1 tsp
Green onion
for garnish
Sesame seeds
for garnish
The Bowl
Steamed white rice
as needed
Shredded cabbage or cucumber slices optional
optional

How We Make It

1
Slow cook the braised pork

Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, gochujang, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and rice vinegar together. Place the pork in the slow cooker and pour the sauce over it. Cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or high for 4 hours until the pork shreds easily. Shred with two forks and toss in the cooking liquid.

2
Make the spicy stir-fry pork

Mix gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and sesame oil into a marinade. Toss the thinly sliced pork belly in it and let sit 10 minutes. Heat a wok or heavy skillet to screaming hot. Stir-fry the pork in batches — don't overcrowd — for 2 to 3 minutes until caramelized and slightly charred at the edges. This is the spicy crispy layer that makes the bowl.

3
Build the bowl

Rice on the bottom. Add a generous portion of shredded braised pork. Top with a serving of the spicy stir-fry pork. Garnish with sliced green onion, sesame seeds, and a drizzle of any leftover braising liquid. Add shredded cabbage or cucumber slices if you want something fresh to cut the richness.

Quick Info
slow cook4-8 hrs
stir fry15 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Gochujang is the non-negotiable here — find it in the Asian aisle or Korean grocery store. The slow-cooker pork keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well. The stir-fry pork is best fresh. The crew makes both components separately and assembles bowls through the week.

Crew Tested · Chicken & Indian

BUTTER
CHICKEN

Marinated in yogurt, charred hard in the pan, then dropped into a tomato-cream sauce with butter, garam masala, fenugreek, ginger, and garlic. The fenugreek (kasuri methi) is what makes it taste like the restaurant. Most home versions skip it. Don't. Slow simmer until the sauce goes deep orange and silky. Serve over rice or with garlic naan. The crew eats this with both.

⏱ Marinate: 2 hrs+
Cook: 45 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
methodPan + Braise
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.4 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Marinade
Chicken thighs boneless skinless, cut into chunks
1.5 lbs
Plain yogurt
½ cup
Lemon juice
1 tbsp
Garam masala
1 tsp
Cumin
1 tsp
Turmeric
½ tsp
Chili powder
½ tsp
Salt
1 tsp
Garlic minced
3 cloves
Fresh ginger grated
1 tbsp
The Sauce
Butter
3 tbsp
Onion finely diced
1 large
Garlic minced
4 cloves
Fresh ginger grated
1 tbsp
Garam masala
1.5 tsp
Cumin
1 tsp
Coriander
1 tsp
Tomato passata or crushed tomatoes
1 cup
Heavy cream
¾ cup
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
1 tbsp
Salt & sugar
to taste

How We Make It

1
Marinate — 2 hours minimum, overnight preferred

Mix all marinade ingredients together and coat the chicken chunks thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, overnight if you can. The yogurt and acid tenderize the chicken; the spices build flavor that goes all the way through.

2
Char the chicken

Heat a heavy pan or cast iron to high heat with a tablespoon of oil. Cook the marinated chicken in batches, getting char on each piece — 2 to 3 minutes per side. The chicken will still be slightly undercooked in the center at this point. It finishes in the sauce. Pull out and set aside.

// The char is not optional. Those dark bits carry flavor that the sauce absorbs. Light golden chicken doesn't have the same depth.
3
Build the sauce

In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until deeply golden — not just soft, actually golden. Add garlic and ginger, cook 2 minutes. Add garam masala, cumin, and coriander, stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato darkens and the oil separates slightly.

4
Add cream, chicken, and fenugreek

Pour in the cream and stir to combine. Add the charred chicken back in. Simmer on low for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has deepened in color. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms and stir it in at the very end. Season with salt and a small pinch of sugar if the sauce needs it.

// The kasuri methi goes in last, off the heat or at a very low simmer. It's what gives butter chicken that signature flavor. Don't skip it — this is the ingredient most home versions are missing.
Quick Info
marinate2+ hrs
cook45 min
serves4
Crew Notes

Kasuri methi is dried fenugreek — find it at any Indian grocery or on Amazon. The crew serves this over basmati rice with garlic naan. Leftovers taste even better the next day. Freezes well for up to 3 months.

Crew Tested · Soup & Italian-American

ZUPPA
TOSCANA

Bacon, spicy Italian sausage, 10 garlic cloves, potatoes, kale, chicken broth, and a full cup of whipping cream. Olive Garden charges restaurant prices for something you can build better at home in 45 minutes. The bacon goes in first, renders down, comes out. Then the sausage, then the aromatics, then broth, potatoes, kale, and cream. Season heavy. Add red chili flakes. Eat with bread.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Cook: 30 min
Serves: 8
Quick Stats
typeSoup
methodDutch Oven
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Soup
Bacon chopped
16 oz
Spicy Italian sausage
1 lb
Garlic minced
10 cloves
Medium onion finely diced
1
Chicken broth
4 cups
Water
4 cups
Russet potatoes chopped
5 medium
Kale leaves stripped and chopped
1 bundle (~4 cups)
Heavy whipping cream
1 cup
Salt, black pepper, red chili flakes
generous

How We Make It

1
Render the bacon

Add the chopped bacon to a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sauté for 5 to 7 minutes until browned and crispy. Remove to a paper-towel-lined plate. Drain most of the rendered fat from the pot, leaving about 1 tablespoon behind.

2
Brown the sausage

Add the Italian sausage to the pot, breaking it into small pieces with a spatula. Cook until browned and cooked through — about 5 minutes. Remove to the same paper towel plate as the bacon. Leave the rendered flavor behind in the pot.

3
Build the base

Add the diced onion to the same pot and sauté for 5 minutes until soft and golden. Add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute more until fragrant.

4
Add broth and potatoes

Pour in 4 cups of chicken broth and 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil. Add the chopped potatoes and cook for 13 to 14 minutes until easily pierced with a fork. Don't let them get so soft they fall apart — they should hold their shape in the soup.

5
Kale, sausage, cream

When potatoes are nearly done, add the chopped kale and cooked sausage. Bring back to a light boil. Stir in the whipping cream. Bring to a boil once more, then pull off the heat. Season generously with salt, black pepper, and red chili flakes. The bacon goes back in just before serving.

Quick Info
prep15 min
cook30 min
serves8
Crew Notes

Use spicy Italian sausage — mild makes a fundamentally different soup. Kale wilts more as it sits; if making ahead, add the kale only when reheating. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Serve with crusty bread to soak up the cream broth. This is a cold weather crew staple.

Crew Tested · Baking & Copycat

NOTHING
BUNDT CAKE
(VANILLA)

The crew cracked the $40 bundt. White cake mix, instant vanilla pudding, sour cream, egg whites, oil — one bowl, 45 minutes, done. The sour cream is the moisture secret. The pudding powder goes in dry, don't make it first. Cream cheese frosting piped in the NBC signature ribbon pattern with a plastic bag. It tastes like the real thing because it basically is.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Bake: 45 min
14 slices
Quick Stats
typeBundt Cake
methodOven · 350°F
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Cake
White cake mix 1 package, any brand
1 box (15.25 oz)
Instant vanilla pudding DRY — don't make it
3.9 oz box
Sour cream
¾ cup
Egg whites or 4 whole eggs (slightly more yellow)
4 large
Water
½ cup
Vegetable or canola oil
½ cup
Cream Cheese Frosting
Cream cheese room temperature
8 oz
Butter softened
2 tbsp
Powdered sugar
2 cups
Vanilla extract
1½ tsp

How We Make It

1
Preheat and prep the pan

Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease and flour every crevice of a 9.5-inch bundt pan thoroughly. Missing a spot means the cake sticks and your ribbon presentation is ruined. The crew uses butter and flour, then gives it a sharp tap to shake off excess.

2
Mix the cake batter

In a large bowl, combine the dry pudding powder, cake mix, sour cream, egg whites, water, and oil. Mix until just combined — don't use a stand mixer and don't overmix. Overmixed cake batter goes flat. A spoon works. Pour into the bundt pan and give it a gentle shake to level the batter.

// The pudding goes in DRY as a powder. You're not making pudding — you're adding it as an ingredient. The Greek yogurt sub for sour cream works perfectly too.
3
Bake 40-45 minutes

Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Do not open the oven early. When done, let the cake cool in the pan for EXACTLY 10 minutes — not 8, not 15. Then flip onto a cooling rack. Let it cool completely before frosting.

4
Make the frosting

Beat the room-temperature cream cheese and softened butter on high until light and fluffy. Add powdered sugar and vanilla and continue whipping until smooth. If it's too runny, the butter and cream cheese were too warm — chill the bowl for 20 minutes and try again.

5
Pipe the NBC ribbons

Spoon the frosting into a gallon zip bag and cut one corner to make a hole just under ½ inch. Pipe from the outside edge of the cake toward the center hole in thick ribbons, working around the cake. The NBC signature look is thick cream cheese bands — don't be shy with the frosting.

Quick Info
prep10 min
bake40-45 min
slices14
Crew Notes

Store refrigerated — put toothpicks around the top before wrapping with plastic so the frosting ribbons don't get smashed. Keeps 5 days in the fridge. Swap cake mix + pudding flavor to change the cake — chocolate/chocolate, lemon/lemon, red velvet/vanilla all work.

Crew Tested · Dumplings & Chinese

SOUP
DUMPLINGS
(XLB)

The traditional method takes all day boiling bones. The crew's version uses a gelatin-based soup jelly made overnight — same result, fraction of the effort. The jelly gets chopped into cubes, folded into seasoned pork filling, sealed in dumpling wrappers and steamed for 8 minutes. The gelatin melts into broth inside. You bite the top, sip the soup, then eat the dumpling. That's the move.

Jelly: night before
⏱ Active: 1 hr
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinPork
methodSteam
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Soup Jelly (Night Before)
Chicken stock
2 cups
Light soy sauce
1 tbsp
Dark soy sauce
½ tbsp
Sesame oil
1 tsp
Shaoxing cooking wine
1 tbsp
Salt
1 tsp
White pepper
1 tsp
Chinese 5-spice
1 tsp
Gelatin powder bloomed in ½ cup cold water
12g
Dumpling Filling
Ground pork
250g
Spring onions chopped
5
Chives chopped
30g
Fresh ginger grated, 1 inch
1 inch
Garlic minced
2 cloves
Light soy sauce
1 tbsp
Dark soy sauce
1 tbsp
Salt
1 tsp
Chili oil
1 tsp
Sesame oil
1 tsp
Dumpling wrappers
250g pack

How We Make It

1
Night before: make the soup jelly

Bloom the gelatin: sprinkle it over ½ cup cold water, letting each layer absorb before adding more. Leave 5 minutes until softened. In a saucepan, combine all soup jelly ingredients except the gelatin. Bring to a boil then reduce to a simmer. Add the bloomed gelatin and stir until completely dissolved. Pour into a container and refrigerate overnight (minimum 8 hours). It will set into a firm jelly.

2
Make the filling

In a large bowl, combine ground pork, spring onions, chives, ginger, garlic, soy sauces, salt, chili oil, and sesame oil. Mix until combined. Remove the soup jelly from the fridge, invert onto a cutting board, and chop into small cubes. Gently fold the jelly cubes into the pork filling — don't smash them, you want the cubes mostly intact so they melt evenly inside each dumpling.

// Keep the filling cold at all times. The jelly starts melting if it gets warm. Work with small portions and keep the rest in the fridge.
3
Wrap the dumplings

Place a dumpling wrapper in your palm. Add 1 to 2 teaspoons of filling in the center — make sure each one gets a jelly cube. Wet the edges with a damp finger. Fold the edges inward in small pleats, pinching and rotating as you go to form a pleated top. Twist the final pleat to close. The XLB pleat is a skill — don't worry about perfection, the seal is what matters.

4
Steam 8 minutes

Fill a pan or wok halfway with water and bring to a boil. Place a steamer basket lined with parchment paper (poke a few holes in it) above the water — the water should not touch the dumplings. Steam 6 to 8 dumplings at a time with the lid on for 8 minutes. They're done when the wrapper turns slightly translucent and the dumplings puff up.

5
Serve immediately

Lift with chopsticks from the top pleat. Place in a bowl. Top with chili oil and sliced spring onion. The classic method: bite a small hole in the top, sip the hot broth first, then eat the dumpling. Do not skip this step.

Quick Info
jellyovernight
active~1 hr
steam8 min
Crew Notes

For extra soupy dumplings: set aside ¼ of the jelly cubes and add an extra cube directly into each wrapper before sealing. Freeze uncooked XLB in a single layer on a tray, then bag. Steam from frozen 10-12 minutes. No thawing.

TUCKER'S
CHEX MIX

Tucker's recipe. Three kinds of Chex, pretzels, bagel chips, butter, Worcestershire, seasoned salt, garlic powder, onion powder. Microwave method — 5 to 6 minutes in 2-minute intervals, stir each time, spread on paper towels to cool. The crew keeps a container of this around at all times. It doesn't last long.

Microwave: 6 min

How We Make It

1
Combine the dry mix

In a large microwavable bowl, mix all three Chex cereals, pretzels, and broken bagel chips together. Set aside.

2
Melt the seasoning butter

In a separate small microwavable bowl, microwave the butter uncovered on HIGH for about 40 seconds until melted. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, seasoned salt, garlic powder, and onion powder until fully combined.

3
Coat and microwave

Pour the seasoning butter over the cereal mix and stir until every piece is evenly coated. Microwave uncovered on HIGH for 5 to 6 minutes total, stirring thoroughly every 2 minutes. The mix should get lightly toasted and fragrant.

// Don't skip the stirring intervals. The outer pieces cook faster and will burn while the inside stays bland if you don't mix it through.
4
Cool on paper towels

Spread the hot mix in a single layer on paper towels to cool completely. The paper towels absorb excess butter and help the mix crisp up. Once cooled, transfer to an airtight container. Keeps well for up to a week — if it lasts that long.

AVOCADO
EGG ROLLS

Red onion, fresh cilantro, sun-dried tomatoes, ripe avocado, salt, lime — rolled tight in egg roll wrappers and fried until golden. The sun-dried tomatoes are the move that makes these different from every other avocado egg roll. Cheesecake Factory got famous off this. The crew makes them at home for a fraction of the price.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Fry: 5 min
Makes 8
Quick Stats
typeAppetizer
methodDeep Fry
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Filling
Red onion finely diced
½
Fresh cilantro small bunch, chopped
small bunch
Sun-dried tomatoes oil-packed, drained and chopped
4 oz
Ripe avocados
4
Lime juice
½ lime
Salt
to taste
Egg roll wrappers
8
Oil for frying
enough to fry

How We Make It

1
Make the filling

In a bowl, combine the diced red onion, chopped cilantro, and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Cut the avocados in half, remove the pits, and scoop the flesh directly into the bowl. Squeeze in the lime juice and season with salt. Mash everything together until combined but still chunky — you want texture, not guacamole. Taste and adjust salt.

2
Roll tight

Lay an egg roll wrapper on a flat surface, oriented like a diamond. Spoon about 3 tablespoons of filling into the center. Fold the bottom corner up over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly toward the top corner. Seal the flap with a dab of water. The roll needs to be tight or it opens in the oil.

// Don't overfill. A fat egg roll splits in the fryer. 3 tablespoons is the max — roll them tight and seal well.
3
Fry until golden

Heat oil in a deep pan or pot to 350°F. Fry 2 to 3 egg rolls at a time, seam side down first, turning occasionally, for about 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown all over. Don't overcrowd — they need room to cook evenly without dropping the oil temp. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate.

4
Serve immediately

Slice diagonally and serve hot with the crew's ranch dressing, a cilantro-lime dipping sauce, or a tamarind sauce. Eat them while they're crispy — they soften as they cool.

Quick Info
prep10 min
fry5 min
makes8
Crew Notes

Air fryer version: brush with oil and air fry at 400°F for 8-10 minutes, flipping once. Not quite as crispy but solid. The sun-dried tomatoes are what separates this from every copycat recipe that skips them — don't leave them out.

Crew Fave · Full Detailed Recipe

SINNER
COOKIES

Cold butter, cold eggs, dark brown sugar, two chocolates, cornstarch, instant coffee. Freeze the dough balls for at least 2 hours — mandatory, not optional. Then 350°F for 16 to 18 minutes until the edges go golden and the center stays soft. The crew's most requested baking recipe with full gram weights so there's no guessing.

⏱ Prep: 20 min
Freeze: 2+ hrs
Bake: 16-18 min
Quick Stats
typeCookies
temp350°F
difficultyMedium
crew rating10 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
Wet
Unsalted butter cold, cubed
225g (1 cup)
Dark brown sugar
200g (1 cup)
Granulated sugar
37g (3 tbsp)
Egg + 1 egg yolk COLD
1 + 1 yolk
Vanilla bean paste
1 tbsp
Dry
All-purpose flour
285g (2¼ cups)
Baking soda
¼ tsp
Baking powder
½ tsp
Cornstarch
1 tsp
Salt pinch
pinch
Instant coffee don't skip this
½ tsp
The Chocolate
Semi-sweet chocolate chips
250g (1 cup)
Milk chocolate chunks
125g (½ cup)

How We Make It

1
Beat butter until creamy

Add cold cubed butter to a stand mixer or large bowl. Beat on high for about 2 minutes until creamy. Add dark brown sugar and granulated sugar and beat again for 2 to 3 minutes on high until well combined and slightly lighter in color.

2
Add eggs and vanilla

Add the cold egg and cold egg yolk along with the vanilla bean paste. Beat on high for 3 to 4 minutes until everything is well incorporated. The mixture should look smooth and slightly ribboned. Cold eggs are intentional — they keep the butter from melting and help the cookie hold its shape.

3
Combine dry and add to wet

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cornstarch, salt, and instant coffee. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture. Mix until just combined. Do NOT overmix at this stage — stop the moment you don't see dry flour. Add in both chocolates and fold until just incorporated.

// The instant coffee doesn't make the cookie taste like coffee. It amplifies the chocolate and adds depth. The crew doesn't skip it.
4
Scoop and freeze — mandatory step

Scoop the dough into 6oz balls — tall, not flat. Arrange on a baking sheet and freeze for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best results. This is not optional. Frozen dough bakes slower and more evenly, giving you crispy edges and a gooey soft center. Unfrozen dough spreads flat and bakes through — not what we're after.

5
Bake 16-18 minutes at 350°F

Preheat oven to 350°F. Place 3 to 4 frozen dough balls on a prepared baking sheet, leaving at least 4 inches between each. Bake for 16 to 18 minutes — the edges should be golden and slightly firm, the center still looks soft and slightly underdone. It firms up as it cools. Pull them out before you think they're done. Let cool completely on the pan before moving.

Quick Info
freeze2+ hrs or overnight
bake temp350°F
bake time16-18 min
Crew Notes

The crew keeps a bag of frozen dough balls in the freezer at all times and bakes them from frozen on demand. Frozen dough keeps 3 months. Bake directly from frozen — no thawing. The two-chocolate combination (semi-sweet chips + milk chocolate chunks) is the right call, don't use only one type.

COSTCO
ROTISSERIE
CHICKEN BOWL

The crew's go-to leftover move. Costco rotisserie chicken, leftover rice, fried egg, green onion, soy sauce, and the liquid gold from the chicken bag. That bag stock is why you save it. It goes over the rice and makes the whole bowl. Ten minutes, zero waste, hits every single time. This is not a recipe — this is a skill.

How We Make It

1
Heat the rice with stock

Put leftover rice in a pan or microwave. If using the pan method: add the rice with a splash of the chicken bag stock and heat over medium, stirring until hot and loose. The stock rehydrates the rice and seasons it at the same time. If microwaving: add a splash of stock before covering and heating.

// Save the liquid from the Costco chicken bag. It's concentrated, salty, deeply flavored chicken stock. Pour it over everything in the bowl. This is the secret of the whole recipe.
2
Pull the chicken

Shred the rotisserie chicken — whatever cuts you have. Dark meat is better in this bowl. Warm it briefly in the microwave or in the pan with the rice.

3
Fry the egg

Fry an egg in a buttered pan to your preferred doneness. The crew runs it sunny side up so the yolk breaks over the rice when you cut in. This is the right call.

4
Build the bowl

Rice on the bottom. Chicken on top. Fried egg on the chicken. Sliced green onion over everything. Drizzle soy sauce. If you saved the bag stock, pour a spoonful directly over the bowl. Eat immediately while the egg is still hot.

Crew Tested · Chicken & North African

HARISSA
CHICKEN
MARINADE

The crew's most flavorful chicken marinade in the whole vault. Onion, tomato, parsley, garlic — blended into the yogurt base along with harissa, turmeric, smoked paprika, and lemon. Three pounds of bone-in skin-on chicken thighs marinated overnight. The marinade goes deep. Cook it over high heat so the skin chars while the yogurt crisps up on the outside. It's different from everything else in the vault.

Marinate: overnight
Cook: 30-40 min
Serves: 6
Quick Stats
proteinBone-in Chicken Thighs
methodGrill or Oven
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.6 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Marinade
Small yellow onion quartered
1 (175g)
Small tomatoes quartered
2 (240g)
Fresh parsley torn in half
1 bunch (90g)
Garlic cloves
6 cloves (20g)
0% fat Greek yogurt
1 cup (230g)
Olive oil
2 tbsp (26g)
Harissa paste
3 tbsp regular + ½ cup Mina brand
Lemon zest and juice of half
½ lemon
Turmeric powder
1.5 tbsp (10g)
Smoked paprika
1 tbsp (10g)
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
2 tsp (7g)
The Chicken
Bone-in skin-on chicken thighs
3 lbs (1400g)

How We Make It

1
Blend the marinade

Add the quartered onion, tomatoes, parsley, and garlic to a blender or food processor. Blend until smooth. Add the Greek yogurt, olive oil, harissa paste, lemon zest and juice, turmeric, smoked paprika, and salt. Blend again until everything is fully combined and smooth.

2
Coat and marinate overnight

Score the chicken thighs with a knife — 2 to 3 cuts through the skin down to the bone. This lets the marinade penetrate deep. Pour the marinade over the chicken and coat every piece thoroughly, getting under the skin where possible. Cover and refrigerate overnight. Minimum 4 hours, overnight is better.

// The blended onion and tomato in the yogurt base makes this marinade fundamentally different from a standard yogurt-spice marinade. It's more complex and the fresh vegetable aromatics carry into the meat.
3
Grill or oven-cook high heat

Grill over medium-high heat, skin side down first, for 8 to 10 minutes until charred and releasing cleanly. Flip and cook another 20 to 25 minutes until cooked through (165°F internal). For oven: roast at 425°F skin side up on a rack for 35 to 40 minutes until the yogurt marinade caramelizes and the skin chars. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

Quick Info
marinateovernight
cook30-40 min
serves6
Crew Notes

Mina harissa is worth finding — it's mild enough to use in large quantities without scorching the dish. Serve over Mediterranean yellow rice or with garlic naan. Leftover harissa chicken reheated in a pan is one of the best lunches in the rotation.

Crew Tested · Salads & Beans

CHARRED POBLANO
BLACK BEAN
SALAD

The dressing is the whole point. Deeply charred poblano pepper blended with mayo, lime juice, cilantro, and a splash of water until smooth. That smoky charred pepper flavor carries through every bite. Black beans, diced avocado, red onion, bell pepper — dressed and assembled. The crew runs this as a side, a topping, or eats it straight from the bowl.

⏱ 20 min
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
typeSalad / Side
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.1 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Dressing
Large poblano or 2 Anaheim chilis — deeply charred
1 large
Olive oil
1 tbsp
Water
3 tbsp
Light mayo
2 tbsp
Lime juice
½ lime
Diamond Crystal kosher salt
½ tsp
Fresh cilantro 1 bunch
1 bunch
The Salad
Black beans canned, drained and rinsed
16 oz can
Avocado diced
1
Red onion thinly sliced
¼
Red bell pepper diced
1
Green bell pepper optional
optional

How We Make It

1
Deeply char the poblano

Place the poblano directly over the flame of a gas burner — as high as it will go. Char it on all sides until the skin is blistered and blackened. If you don't have gas, use the broiler on the highest setting, rotating every few minutes. The pepper should look like it's destroyed. That's right. Let it cool slightly, then remove the seeds and most of the charred skin — leaving some char is fine, even better.

// "Deeply char" means it looks burnt. This is intentional. The smoky flavor only comes from real char — a lightly roasted pepper gives you a completely different dressing.
2
Blend the dressing

Add the charred poblano, olive oil, water, mayo, lime juice, salt, and fresh cilantro to a blender. Blend until smooth and fully combined. Taste and adjust — more lime for brightness, more salt to punch up the flavor, more water to thin the consistency. The dressing should be creamy, bright green, and smoky.

3
Build the salad

Add the diced avocado to a bowl and roughly smash it with a spoon — leave chunks for texture, don't go to guacamole. Add the drained beans, sliced red onion, and diced bell peppers. Slowly pour the dressing over everything while stirring, adding as much as you want. Taste and adjust salt.

Quick Info
time20 min
serves4
Crew Notes

The dressing can be made ahead and stored for up to 3 days in the fridge. Dress the salad just before serving — the avocado oxidizes and the beans absorb too much dressing if it sits. This pairs well with grilled chicken, the crew's harissa chicken, or as a topping for tacos.

Crew Tested · Beef & Smoker

CHUCK ROAST
SANDWICH

Coat the chuck roast in Worcestershire sauce and your seasonings of choice. Smoke for 3 hours. Transfer to cast iron with onion, garlic, beef broth, and a can of whole pepperoncini. Back in the smoker for another 3 hours. The pepperoncini braising liquid is what makes this different from every other pulled beef sandwich. Italian-seasoned butter on the French rolls. The crew's weekend project that turns into the best sandwich you've eaten.

⏱ Active: 30 min
Smoke: 6 hrs total
Serves: 8
Quick Stats
proteinChuck Roast
methodSmoker + Braise
difficultyMedium
crew rating9.5 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Roast
Chuck roast
3-4 lbs
Worcestershire sauce for coating
generous coat
Seasonings of choice salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, etc.
generous
The Braise
Onion sliced
1 large
Garlic cloves
5-6 cloves
Beef broth
1-2 cups
Whole pepperoncini canned, with liquid
1 can
Butter + Italian seasoning for rolls
to taste
French rolls
8

How We Make It

1
Season and smoke — 3 hours

Coat the chuck roast generously with Worcestershire sauce on all sides, then season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and anything else you're running. Let it sit 30 minutes. Set the smoker to 250°F and smoke the roast directly on the grates for 3 hours, building color and smoke bark on the exterior.

2
Build the braise

Transfer the smoked roast to a cast iron Dutch oven. Add sliced onion, garlic cloves, beef broth, and the entire can of whole pepperoncini with their liquid. The pepperoncini brine is tangy and slightly spicy — it seasons the braise from the inside out. Cover the pot.

// Don't drain the pepperoncini can. The liquid is half the flavor. It makes this sandwich different from every other braised beef sandwich you've had.
3
Back in the smoker — 3 more hours

Place the covered Dutch oven back in the smoker at 250°F for another 3 hours. The roast braises in the pepperoncini-beef-onion liquid while still picking up smoke on the outside of the pot. When done, the beef should pull apart effortlessly with two forks and be falling-apart tender.

4
Pull and serve on Italian butter rolls

Pull the beef apart with forks into chunks. Mix in some of the braising liquid. Slice the French rolls and toast them. Mix softened butter with Italian seasoning and spread generously on the cut sides of each roll. Pile the pulled chuck roast high and serve with some of the pepperoncini on the side. Serve with extra braising liquid for dipping.

Quick Info
first smoke3 hrs
braise/smoke3 hrs
serves8
Crew Notes

No smoker? Finish the braise in a 300°F oven for 3 hours instead of the second smoke session. You lose the smoke depth but the pepperoncini braise still makes it exceptional. Leftovers keep 4 days and reheat in the braising liquid over low heat.

Crew Tested · Baking & Desserts

S'MORES
COOKIE DOUGH

Melted salted butter, dark brown sugar, vanilla bean paste, espresso powder, flour, baking soda, semisweet chocolate chips, and broken chocolate bar pieces. Each cookie is assembled directly on a large marshmallow sitting on a graham cracker square. The cookie bakes around and over the marshmallow. It's a campfire s'more in cookie form, and it's unreasonable.

⏱ Prep: 15 min
Bake: 10-12 min
Makes: 8
Quick Stats
typeStuffed Cookie
temp350°F
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.3 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Cookie Dough
Salted butter melted
113g (½ cup)
Granulated sugar
67g (⅓ cup)
Dark brown sugar
100g (½ cup)
Vanilla bean paste
15g (1 tbsp)
Espresso powder
½ tsp
All-purpose flour
156g (1¼ cups)
Baking soda
½ tsp
Large egg room temperature
1
Semisweet chocolate chips
170g (1 cup)
Chocolate bar pieces
85g (½ cup)
For Assembly
Large marshmallows
8
Graham cracker squares
8

How We Make It

1
Make the dough

Whisk melted butter, granulated sugar, dark brown sugar, vanilla bean paste, and espresso powder together until combined. Add the egg and mix until smooth. Add flour and baking soda and stir until just combined. Fold in chocolate chips and chocolate bar pieces. The dough will be soft from the melted butter — refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes to firm it up slightly before scooping.

2
Preheat and set up

Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment. Place 8 graham cracker squares on the pan. Set one large marshmallow in the center of each cracker.

3
Scoop dough over each marshmallow

Scoop a generous portion of dough and flatten it slightly in your palm. Press it down and around each marshmallow, encasing it partially — the marshmallow doesn't need to be completely covered. The cookie bakes around it. Press a few extra chocolate pieces on top if you want.

// The marshmallow expands in the oven and puffs up through the cookie. Don't fully encase it or it'll have nowhere to go. Leave it slightly exposed at the top.
4
Bake 10-12 minutes

Bake at 350°F for 10 to 12 minutes until the cookie edges are set and lightly golden. The center will look underdone — it firms as it cools. Don't overbake or the marshmallow will deflate and the cookie will go dry. Let cool on the pan for 5 minutes before moving.

Quick Info
prep15 min
bake10-12 min
makes8
Crew Notes

Best eaten warm — the marshmallow stays gooey for about 20 minutes after baking. The chocolate bar pieces between the cookie and the graham cracker melt into the bottom layer. Don't eat these fully cooled — reheat in a 300°F oven for 3 minutes if needed.

Crew Tested · Chicken & BBQ

BBQ
GRILLED
CHICKEN

Honey, mustard, garlic, onion powder, vinegar, olive oil. Coat the thighs, roast at 450°F for 25 to 30 minutes. That's it. The honey caramelizes on the outside, the mustard gives it punch, and the vinegar keeps it from being cloying. Simple, reliable, and the crew has been making this on repeat for months.

⏱ Prep: 5 min
Roast: 25-30 min at 450°F
Serves: 4
Quick Stats
proteinChicken Thighs
methodOven / Grill
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.0 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Marinade
Garlic cloves grated or minced
3-4 cloves
Honey
⅓ cup
Mustard
⅓ cup
Kosher salt
pinch
Black pepper
to taste
Onion powder
¼ tsp
Vinegar apple cider or white
2-3 tsp
Olive oil
⅓ to ½ cup
Boneless skinless chicken thighs
1½ to 2 lbs

How We Make It

1
Mix the marinade

Whisk together grated garlic, honey, mustard, salt, pepper, onion powder, vinegar, and olive oil until combined. Taste it — it should be sweet, tangy, and garlicky. Adjust to your preference.

2
Coat the chicken

Pour the marinade over the chicken thighs and coat every piece thoroughly. Let them sit at room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 4 hours. The longer they sit, the deeper the flavor goes.

3
Roast at 450°F for 25-30 minutes

Preheat oven to 450°F. Arrange the chicken thighs on a lined baking sheet or cast iron in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until cooked through and the honey has caramelized on the exterior. The edges will char slightly — that's the move. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

// 450°F is the right temperature. Lower heat won't caramelize the honey properly and you get pale, steamed chicken. Go hot.
Quick Info
prep5 min
roast25-30 min
temp450°F
Crew Notes

Works equally well on the grill — medium-high heat, 5-6 minutes per side. Also works with bone-in thighs at the same temp but add 10-15 minutes. Serve with rice, roasted potatoes, or in a wrap with the crew's ranch dressing.

Crew Tested · Texas BBQ

TEXAS
BBQ SAUCE

Not ketchup-based — tomato paste base with sautéed onion and garlic, honey, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, Dijon, Worcestershire, chili powder, coriander, celery salt. Simmer for 25 minutes until it thickens slightly. Puree if you want smooth, leave it if you want texture. Let it rest overnight before using. The flavor changes completely after 24 hours in the fridge.

⏱ Prep: 10 min
Simmer: 25 min
Makes ~3 cups
Quick Stats
typeBBQ Sauce
baseTomato Paste
difficultyEasy
crew rating9.2 / 10

Ingredients

Ingredients
The Sauce
Butter
2 tbsp
Sweet onion superfine dice
½
Garlic minced
2 cloves
Tomato paste
6 oz
Water
2½ cups
Brown sugar
½ cup
Honey
½ cup
Apple cider vinegar
¼ cup
Fresh lemon juice
2 tbsp
Worcestershire sauce
2 tbsp
Dijon mustard
2 tbsp
Chili powder
1 tbsp + 1 tsp
Celery salt
2 tsp
Cracked black pepper
2 tsp
Salt
2 tsp
Ground coriander
1 tsp

How We Make It

1
Soften the onion and garlic

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the superfine-diced onion and garlic. Cook, stirring frequently, for about 4 minutes until the onion is translucent and soft. This step builds the base flavor — don't skip it or rush it.

2
Add remaining ingredients and simmer

Whisk in all remaining ingredients — tomato paste, water, brown sugar, honey, apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, Worcestershire, Dijon, chili powder, celery salt, pepper, salt, and coriander. Stir until combined. Bring to just a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce will start very thin and slowly thicken.

3
Blend or leave it

Turn off the heat and let the sauce cool. For a smooth sauce: carefully transfer to a blender, seal tightly, and blend on high until smooth. For a textured sauce with visible onion: leave it as is. Both are valid.

4
Rest overnight before using

Store in a sealed jar in the fridge. This sauce is genuinely better the next day after the flavors meld. Use on brisket, ribs, pulled pork, or burgers. Keeps 2 weeks refrigerated.

// Make it the day before you need it. The 24-hour rest is what separates this from a sauce that just tastes like ingredients.
Quick Info
prep10 min
simmer25 min
makes~3 cups
keeps2 weeks
Crew Notes

Use this on the crew's Texas Smoked Pulled Pork and on the Chuck Roast Sandwich. Also excellent on grilled chicken thighs. The tomato paste base gives it more depth than ketchup-based sauces and it doesn't overpower smoked meats.
